taglineFr: La raclette : de gauche ou de droite ? Vote, regarde la salle se déchirer, puis débats.
taglineEn: Is brunch left-coded or right-coded? Vote, watch the room split, then argue it out.

phases.description: phaseKey vote:r{n}. The item card (huge emoji + text) fills the screen; each player taps one of two big axis buttons (FR 'De gauche'/'De droite', EN 'Left-coded'/'Right-coded' — labels come from the pack's axis field). Votes go into a HIDDEN buffer (synthesis §1.5 convention: owner-only echo myVote = votes[viewer] ?? null, never visible to others pre-reveal). Early-resolve when allActed over the connected player set. Timeout (deadline event): resolve with submitted votes only — non-voters score 0 this round and never block the room.

phaseKey reveal:r{n}. Atomic reveal in one broadcast: split bars with live-count percentages, avatar chips stacked under each side (unless params.anonymousVotes), majority side crowned, '+1' animation on majority voters. Exact tie shows the 'Égalité parfaite / Dead even' sticker and awards nothing. Pure timed beat — no input accepted; deadline auto-advances to debate (or skips straight to next round / over when params.debateMs = 0). Emits analytics round_revealed.

phaseKey debate:r{n}. Phones show the item's debateStarter one-liner as argument fuel plus the countdown; the talking happens in the room. Anyone may tap 'On passe / Next'; when strictly more than params.debateSkipThreshold (0.5) of CONNECTED players have tapped (allActed-style quorum over the connected set — disconnected players are excluded so they can never stall or distort the quorum), the phase ends early. Timeout (deadline event): advance to next round, or to 'over' after round totalRounds. Emits analytics round_completed at this boundary (the shell's ad-cadence signal, synthesis §5.4).

phaseKey 'over' (terminal, untimed — phaseDurationMs returns null). Scoreboard: cumulative herd scores, winner = 'le plus dans le sens du vent / most in tune with the room'. One non-scoring superlative from state.minorityCount: 'L'esprit contraire / The Contrarian' for the player most often in the minority (display-only, never affects points — funny never cruel). gameOver effect emits defensively cloned final scores per the tracer invariant.

contentItemShape: One pack item = { id: string (kebab-case, unique in pack, e.g. "raclette"); text: {fr, en} (the word/object/behavior being judged — short noun phrase, <= 80 chars, rendered huge on the vote card); emoji: string (single emoji, the card's hero visual); category: "food" | "lifestyle" | "tech" | "culture" | "sport" | "behavior" (curation/curriculum metadata, reducer ignores it); spicyLevel: 0 | 1 | 2 (per-item rating; items above the config's allowed tier are never drawn); debateStarter: {fr, en} (one playful one-liner, <= 120 chars, shown during the debate phase to fuel arguments — never names real parties/politicians) }. Pack-level data additionally carries: axis: { left: {fr, en}, right: {fr, en} } (default FR "De gauche"/"De droite", EN "Left-coded"/"Right-coded" — the two vote-button labels, pack-defined so sibling packs can mint non-political axes config-only) and locale per the single-locale pack rule (synthesis §3.1): the bilingual authoring source is split at build time into sibling packs gauche-droite-fr and gauche-droite-en following the pack-family convention (template-architecture §2.7); items are NOT translated 1:1 between locales — each locale gets a culturally native item set. Sizing lint (synthesis §3.5): >= totalRounds (7) items per allowed spicy tier, init shuffles with the seeded RNG and caps totalRounds at pool length like tracer.

recommendations.question: How should the EN pack culturally adapt left/right humor (the brief's explicit open question)?
recommendations.recommendation: Use the EN-native form of the exact same meme: axis labels 'Left-coded' / 'Right-coded' (live TikTok slang), and a fully localized item set (oat-milk lattes, lifted pickup trucks, golf, thrifting, bottomless brunch) instead of translating French items. Ship as the sibling pack gauche-droite-en under the pack-family + shell locale-resolution convention (template-architecture §2.7); stage the EN config at rolloutPct 5 and watch completion/abandon analytics before promoting.
recommendations.why: A 1:1 translation of 'la raclette' lands flat outside France; '-coded' carries the identical playful political-aesthetic judgment in EN without invoking actual party politics, which keeps the 'funny never cruel' tone portable across countries.

recommendations.question: Does the vote score anything, and exactly how?
recommendations.recommendation: Herd scoring: at resolve, count L and R over SUBMITTED votes only; if L > R every 'left' voter gets +pointsMajority (1), symmetric for R; exact tie (including the zero-votes degenerate case) awards pointsTie (0) and shows the 'Dead even' splash; timeout non-voters always get 0. Additionally increment a non-scoring state.minorityCount for minority voters, used only for the end-screen 'Contrarian' superlative.
recommendations.why: Rewarding reading the room is the meme's core skill and keeps the leaderboard meaningful under the placement-XP convention (synthesis §1.7); the minority is never penalized below 0, so being the lone weirdo who thinks croissants are right-coded is a badge, not a punishment.

recommendations.question: Are individual votes public at reveal?
recommendations.recommendation: Public by default (avatar chips under each side), with an anonymousVotes param (default false) reserved for future spicy packs.
recommendations.why: 'WHO voted that raclette is right-wing?!' is the entire debate fuel — the stakes are cheese and scooters, not secrets, so public votes maximize the in-room moment at zero social cost.

recommendations.question: How does the debate phase end without a passive/disconnected player ever blocking?
recommendations.recommendation: Hard debateMs deadline (35s) guaranteed by the shell alarm, plus an early-exit when > 50% of CONNECTED players tap 'On passe / Next' (quorum computed over the connected-filtered expected set, synthesis §1.3).
recommendations.why: The deadline satisfies the platform liveness rule by construction; majority-skip keeps pacing TikTok-native when an item lands flat instead of forcing 35 seconds of dead air.

recommendations.question: Is this VOTE as-is, or a template extension?
recommendations.recommendation: Ship as VOTE@2 with three small additive params: choiceMode: 'player' | 'option' (tracer's action targets a PlayerId; this game submits one of two pack-defined option ids), debateMs (0 disables the new debate phase), and the majority-scoring branch. Same skeleton, phaseKey discipline, and hidden-buffer convention as tracer; bundle it with the already-planned revealStyle/selfVoteAllowed VOTE generalization (template-architecture §5.3).
recommendations.why: Per the §3.2 effort taxonomy this is 'new-params, small' (~1–2 days), and the option-vote branch permanently unlocks a whole family of binary-judgment / would-you-rather games as config-only catalog entries afterwards.

recommendations.question: Show a 'what the internet thinks' percentage at reveal?
recommendations.recommendation: Defer to v2. If wanted later, pre-compute a crowdPct per item in the offline content pipeline and store it as pack data (flipping needsOfflineAiPipeline to true for that pack) — never fetched or computed at runtime.
recommendations.why: Fun extra beat, but it adds factual-claim and freshness risk; the core vote-split-debate loop stands entirely on its own.

risks: Political divisiveness drift: the format flirts with real politics. Hard editorial rule — items are only objects, foods, and behaviors; never parties, politicians, elections, or live legislation; debateStarters stay absurd. Enforce via the pack safety gate (template-architecture §6.3) plus the human playtest gate before any rollout promotion.

Not literally zero-code: requires the small VOTE@2 extension (choiceMode 'option' action branch, debate phase + skip quorum, majority-scoring resolver, split-bar reveal layout in the client GameClient). Small per the §3.2 taxonomy, but it must land before this config can ship — schedule it with the planned revealStyle generalization.

Even-sized small rooms tie often (4 players splitting 2–2), producing scoreless rounds. Acceptable as a running joke ('perfectly balanced'), but monitor tie rate via round_revealed analytics; if ties exceed ~30% of rounds, consider a tie=+1-to-all variant param rather than changing the core rule.

Debate dead-air with shy groups: mitigated by the debateStarter one-liner and the majority-skip, but playtest whether 35s is too long for cold groups (host-tunable debateMs is a candidate for the future hostTunable allowlist, template-architecture §7 Q4).

Trend decay: items like e-scooters date within months. Rely on KV pack versioning (synthesis §3.2) for monthly content refreshes with no deploy; keep item categories balanced so a stale tech item never dominates a draw.

EN meme-transfer uncertainty: 'left-coded/right-coded' is strong in US/UK Gen Z but weaker elsewhere in EN markets; the staged rolloutPct path plus per-locale packs contain the blast radius, and a non-political sibling axis (e.g. 'Boomer-coded or Gen Z-coded') is a pure content fallback on the same template.

taglineFr: Deux choix, zéro échappatoire. Devine le camp de tes potes !
taglineEn: Two options, no escape. Call which side the room picks!

phases.description: phaseKey `choose:r{n}`. The dilemma card shows Option A vs Option B ('Tu préfères… / Would you rather…'). Each player makes TWO taps on one screen: (1) their own pick (A or B), (2) their prediction of the room's majority (A or B). The client submits both as ONE atomic action `{ pick: 'A'|'B', predict: 'A'|'B' }` into the HIDDEN buffer (HiddenBuffer convention: never in any non-owner view; owner echo is `buffer[viewer] ?? null`). Early-advance when allActed(connected, buffer) — disconnected players are excluded from `expected` and can never block. TIMEOUT at deadline: players who didn't submit are simply excluded from the tally, score 0 this round, and are shown as 'asleep' on the reveal; the round resolves with whatever was buffered.

phaseKey `reveal:r{n}`. Atomic promotion of the hidden buffer to public view: animated split bar (e.g. 70% / 30%) with player avatars stacked under the option they picked — names attached, because the debate IS the game. SCORING (exact): the majority option = the option with STRICTLY more submitted picks. Every player whose `predict` equals the majority option gains +1 (`predictCorrectPoints`), shown as a badge on their avatar. Your own pick NEVER scores. If the split is a perfect tie, NO prediction points are awarded and a celebratory 'PERFECT SPLIT — ÉGALITÉ PARFAITE' banner plays instead. Emits `round_completed` analytics at this boundary (shell keys its interstitial off the phaseKey transition, not the effect). DEADLINE auto-advances to `choose:r{n+1}` or to `over` after totalRounds — a passive room never stalls; debate spills into the next round's 15s if they're still arguing.

phaseKey `over`, untimed (phaseDurationMs returns null). Terminal podium: final prediction scores, 'Oracle of the group' crown for 1st. Emits the `gameOver` effect with a defensively CLONED scores map (never aliasing live state). The shell converts placement into session XP per the cross-game convention.

contentItemShape: One content-pack item = one dilemma. Authoring shape (bilingual; the publish pipeline splits it into single-locale packs `tu-preferes-fr` / `tu-preferes-en` per the platform `data.locale` convention, shell resolves locale at startGame): { "id": string (kebab-case, unique in pack), "optionA": { "fr": string, "en": string } (≤90 chars, phrased to complete 'Tu préfères… / Would you rather…'), "optionB": { "fr": string, "en": string } (same constraints; A and B must be comparably attractive/awful so the room genuinely splits), "category": "absurd" | "food" | "social" | "deep" | "spicy", "spicyLevel": 0 | 1 | 2 (pack-level tone must be >= max item level; spicy items only ship in the 18+ sibling pack), "tags"?: string[] (curation metadata, ignored by the reducer). No pre-computed AI values are needed: the majority is computed deterministically at runtime from the room's own votes. Pool sizing lint: >= 3 × totalRounds drawable items per category mix (~200+ items for a healthy pack); init shuffles with the seeded RNG and caps totalRounds at pool length like tracer.

recommendations.question: Which scoring model is best (the brief's open ask: include 'predict the majority' and pick the winner)?
recommendations.recommendation: Predict-the-majority, exactly: +1 per correct strict-majority prediction; your own pick NEVER scores; tie = no points. Rejected alternatives: (a) majority-conformity (+1 for being in the majority) — punishes hot takes and incentivizes lying about your pick, killing the debate; (b) minority-reward — incentivizes fake contrarian picks; (c) contrarian-oracle bonus (+2 if you predict correctly while personally in the minority) — perverse incentive to deliberately pick the side you predict will lose.
recommendations.why: Predict-majority is the only model where the dominant strategy is total honesty about your own pick (it's score-neutral) while adding a real skill axis — knowing your friends. It also matches the brief faithfully: choice stays pure expression, the reveal stays the debate fuel, and the points ride on top without distorting either.

recommendations.question: What happens on a tie (no strict majority)?
recommendations.recommendation: Nobody scores; the reveal plays a celebratory 'PERFECT SPLIT' banner instead of prediction badges.
recommendations.why: Deterministic and trivial to reduce; it converts the scoring dead-end into the round's best moment (a perfectly divisive dilemma is content-pack success, not failure). Frequent at even player counts, hence the rule must be loud and fun, not silent.

recommendations.question: Are picks revealed publicly (with names) or only as anonymous percentages?
recommendations.recommendation: Public: avatars stack under the option they chose, and correct predictors get a visible +1 badge. Keep a `publicPicks` param so future 18+ spicy configs can flip to anonymous percentages-only.
recommendations.why: The brief's core loop is 'on révèle la répartition, débat' — debate needs names ('TOI t'as choisi ça ?!'). At spicyLevel 0–1 nothing is sensitive; the param future-proofs spicy packs where anonymity protects the 'funny never cruel' line.

recommendations.question: Is this genuinely a zero-code config on VOTE?
recommendations.recommendation: Almost. Ship a small VOTE@2 generalization first: `ballotKind: 'players' | 'options'` (ballot over content-supplied A/B instead of the roster, so `selfVoteAllowed` is moot) plus a `scoring: 'vote-leader' | 'predict-majority'` branch with a second field in the hidden buffer. Land it alongside the already-planned `revealStyle`/`selfVoteAllowed` VOTE param work (template-architecture §3.2/§5.3).
recommendations.why: tracer's reducer validates `action.target` against the player roster, so option-ballots are a new (small) reducer/view branch — the 'new-params' effort class, ~1–2 days, same pattern as Pass the Bloop's flip-one-by-one. After VOTE@2, every future Tu Préfères variant (themed packs, spicy pack) is pure Cadence B: KV config + R2 pack, no deploy.

recommendations.question: Single choose phase or split pick-then-predict phases?
recommendations.recommendation: One `choose` phase; one atomic action `{ pick, predict }`; two-tap UI where the second tap auto-submits.
recommendations.why: Halves timer overhead (keeps a round at ~30s, TikTok-native), keeps a single hidden buffer + single allActed check, and avoids extra phaseKey churn/alarm re-arms. A 15s window is comfortably enough for two taps.

recommendations.question: Minimum players?
recommendations.recommendation: Config minPlayers 3 (module floor stays 2 per VOTE template bounds; the config tightens per template-architecture §2.6).
recommendations.why: At 2 players, any disagreement is a tie and prediction collapses into 'do we agree?' — degenerate. At 3+ (especially odd counts) a strict majority exists whenever everyone submits, so prediction scoring always has teeth.

recommendations.question: Streaks or bonus multipliers?
recommendations.recommendation: Defer to v2: a param-gated fire-streak (+1 bonus on every 3rd consecutive correct prediction). Not in the launch config.
recommendations.why: Great TikTok-native juice and deterministic (one per-player streak counter in state), but it adds reducer state beyond the quick-win scope; the whole point of this game is shipping fast on VOTE@2.

recommendations.question: Spicy content?
recommendations.recommendation: Launch with the classic pack only (spicyLevel 0). Ship 'tu-preferes-spicy' later as a SIBLING catalog config: same template, `tone:'spicy'`, `minAge:18`, separate pack ids, `publicPicks:false`.
recommendations.why: The game_config schema already enforces spicy ⇒ minAge ≥ 18 (refinement (c)); a sibling config is zero extra code and keeps the all-ages tile clean on Home.

risks: Not literally zero-code today: requires the small VOTE@2 `ballotKind:'options'` + `scoring:'predict-majority'` generalization (tracer's reducer currently ballots over the player roster). Bounded (~1-2 days, 'new-params' class) but it must ship before the config can go live.

Even player counts tie often, which zeroes prediction points; mitigated by the PERFECT SPLIT celebration and by recommending odd-count rooms, but a night of 4-player ties could feel score-starved — monitor round_completed analytics and consider the v2 streak bonus as compensation.
Two decisions in one 15s phase adds tap friction; the UI must make pick-then-predict a single fluid gesture (second tap auto-submits) or slow players will hit the timeout path often.
Fixed 15s reveal can cut a great debate short (or drag on a dud item); social pacing risk — a future hostTunable 'extend debate' toggle (template-architecture §7 Q4) is the relief valve, not in v1.

Content is everything: options must be genuinely balanced to split the room; lopsided dilemmas make prediction trivial and debate dead. Author/curate to ≥3× totalRounds per category mix (~200+ items) and require natural, non-machine-translated FR and EN (AI gate step 5 human pass if AI-assisted).

Redaction surface: picks AND predictions are HIDDEN buffer fields until the atomic reveal; the owner-echo must be `buffer[viewer] ?? null` only, and the leakedSecrets audit + per-viewer view tests are mandatory (a leaked early tally would let players game their prediction).

Anti-pattern guard: a player could stall submitting to see others' choices — impossible by design (buffer hidden, hasVoted booleans only, deadline resolves regardless), but the view must expose only hasSubmitted flags, never partial counts, or the guard breaks.

taglineFr: La culture gé au doigt mouillé : personne ne sait, le plus proche rafle tout.
taglineEn: Trivia where nobody knows the answer — closest guess takes it all.

phases.description: phaseKey `guess:r{n}`. An off-beat culture-gé question with a verified NUMERIC answer is shown (e.g. 'Shortest scheduled commercial flight, in seconds?'). Each player secretly types an integer on a big numeric keypad (max 9 digits, integers only). Guesses live in a HIDDEN buffer `guesses: Record<PlayerId, number>` (synthesis §1.5 HiddenBuffer convention); owner echo is `guesses[viewer] ?? null`, never visible to others. Early-advance when allActed(connectedPlayers) — all connected players submitted. Timeout: on deadline, players who didn't submit simply have no entry (0 pts this round); a disconnected or passive player NEVER blocks the room.

phaseKey `reveal:r{n}`. Atomic promotion of the hidden buffer: all guesses pop onto an animated number line (client-side animation, no extra server beats), then the TRUE answer slams in, then points fly. Scoring (exact): rank answerers by |guess − answer| ascending, competition ranking — 1st: 100, 2nd: 50, 3rd: 25, everyone else 0; ties share the rank's points and skip the next rank (two tied closest → both 100, next player gets 25); exact hit adds +50 'Pile !' bonus; in the final round all points are ×2 (finalRoundMultiplier). The bilingual funFact punchline is shown ('The T-Rex is closer in time to your phone than to the Stegosaurus'). Advance on deadline only; emits `round_completed` analytics — this transition is the shell's ad-cue boundary (synthesis §5.4).

phaseKey `over`, untimed (phaseDurationMs returns null). Final podium with per-match scores; `gameOver` effect carries a defensively CLONED scores map (gameOver() kit helper, synthesis §1.7). Shell shows the interstitial + replay CTA. Session leaderboard XP is placement-based per platform convention, not raw points.

contentItemShape: One pack item = one verified numeric-estimation question. Shape: { id: string (kebab slug), question: { fr, en }, answer: integer (canonical verified truth — the ONLY scoring input, pre-computed offline, never AI at runtime), unit: { fr, en } | null (e.g. {fr:'secondes',en:'seconds'}; null for years), format: 'plain' | 'year' (year renders the reveal as a timeline), scale: 'linear' | 'log' (number-line rendering hint for huge-range answers), funFact: { fr, en } (the reveal punchline — this is where the 'original culture gé' lives; doubles as the answer's justification to settle arguments), tags: string[], difficulty: 1|2|3, spicy: 0|1|2, verifiedAt: 'YYYY-MM' (fact-check stamp), source: string (authoring-only provenance, never shown to players) }. Items are AUTHORED bilingually; the publish pipeline splits them into single-locale packs `quizz-culture-ge-fr` / `quizz-culture-ge-en` per synthesis §3.1 (one pack id = one locale, shell-resolved at startGame). Sizing lint (synthesis §3.5): ≥ totalRounds × 3 items per difficulty tier so a max session never repeats. Hard authoring rule: only time-stable facts — no live populations, prices, or breakable records.

recommendations.question: The brief demands an 'original' general-culture quiz and asks to pick ONE main twist format — which one wins?
recommendations.recommendation: Main format = Twist A, 'closest wins' numeric estimation: every question has a verified numeric answer; everyone secretly types a number; closest takes the round. Original questions = off-beat verifiable numbers + a punchline funFact, not 'capital of France'.
recommendations.why: It removes trivia's core flaw for parties: nobody is ever blocked by not knowing — guessing IS the game, so a 2-player room and a 16-player room both stay live. Zero free-text moderation surface (numeric keypad only), trivially deterministic pure-reducer scoring, and the all-guesses-on-a-number-line reveal is the strongest shareable TikTok moment of the three candidates.

recommendations.question: What was Twist B and why is it not the main format?
recommendations.recommendation: Twist B = 'fool the others' à la Fibbage: each player writes a fake answer to an obscure question; fakes + truth are shuffled; everyone votes; +80 for finding the truth, +60 per player fooled by your fake. Ship it as a v2 mode 'fool' on this same INPUT_GUESS template and catalog entry.
recommendations.why: Highest comedy ceiling, but it is the platform's heaviest free-text surface: it needs the DO obscenity filter path (synthesis §1.8), normalizeText collision handling (fake == truth, duplicate fakes), and a vote sub-phase. Template-architecture §5.3 says battle-test gameplay-text moderation before leaning on it — closest-number ships sooner and safer.

recommendations.question: What was Twist C?
recommendations.recommendation: Twist C = 'Le Piège' (hivemind trap): multiple-choice where the pack pre-computes a trap distractor; you score for being right AND for predicting which option the room's majority picks. Keep as a later content-pack flavor, not the main format.
recommendations.why: Weakest differentiation — MCQ still feels like generic trivia — and it depends on offline-pre-computed distractor quality, the hardest content to generate well. The predict-the-room half is fun but is essentially Hot Seat's mechanic; not worth fragmenting the launch.

recommendations.question: Does this fit an existing template, and what code does it actually need?
recommendations.recommendation: Template = INPUT_GUESS, as a third mode 'closest-number' alongside the designed 'blitz' and 'collab-one-word' (the modes-in-one-template pattern, template-architecture §2.4/§3.3). Extend templateParamsSchema(INPUT_GUESS) with mode 'closest-number' + the params object above. Build closest-number FIRST when INPUT_GUESS lands.
recommendations.why: It is new-params effort (one reveal-resolver branch ranking |guess − answer|, plus a numeric-keypad input view), not a new template — phases, HiddenBuffer, allActed, phaseKey discipline are the template skeleton. It is also the simplest of the three modes (no text, no peer-tap validation, no moderation), so it de-risks the INPUT_GUESS skeleton before the text modes.

recommendations.question: Exact scoring and anti-runaway balance?
recommendations.recommendation: Per round: rank connected answerers by |guess − answer|; competition ranking with shared ties — 100/50/25/0; exact hit +50 'Pile !'; final round ×2 via finalRoundMultiplier; no answer = 0 and never blocks (allActed over connectedPlayers). Keep bustIfOver=false at launch; flip it on later in a themed 'Juste Prix' sibling config (price-is-right over-bid elimination).
recommendations.why: A flat top-3 payout keeps every round swingy at any player count, the exact-hit bonus creates scream moments, and the ×2 finale keeps trailing players mathematically alive. Bust-if-over is iconic but brutal for casuals — perfect as a config-only variant, which costs nothing once the param exists.

recommendations.question: How do we keep 'culture gé' original at scale without runtime AI?
recommendations.recommendation: needsOfflineAiPipeline=true: AI generates estimation questions + funFact punchlines OFFLINE; every item carries answer, source, verifiedAt; the pack passes the template-architecture §6 gate (schema, sizing lint, profanity scan, replay smoke, human fact-check) before enabled:true at rolloutPct 5. Hard rule: time-stable facts only; corrections ship as immutable pack version bumps via the KV kill switch.
recommendations.why: The 'original' feel is 100% a content problem, which is exactly what the platform's offline-pack + staged-rollout machinery is for. Runtime stays a pure deterministic reducer; a wrong viral answer is fixed by a KV edit, no deploy.

risks: INPUT_GUESS is the one unbuilt template (build #5 in the synthesis §4 order): this game cannot ship config-only today. Mitigation: closest-number is the simplest mode — schedule it as the FIRST mode when INPUT_GUESS is built, and the Fibbage 'fool' mode after the text-moderation path is hardened.

Fact drift: numeric answers can silently become wrong (records broken, counts updated). Mitigation: time-stable-facts authoring rule, verifiedAt stamp + source on every item, immutable pack versioning with the KV kill switch for corrections — but a viral wrong answer is a reputational hit, so the human fact-check gate is non-negotiable.
Disputed answers spark room arguments. Mitigation: every funFact doubles as the answer's justification; the offline gate rejects any question whose answer has credible competing values.

Huge-range answers (millions vs single digits) can make the number-line reveal unreadable and invite troll inputs. Mitigation: per-item scale:'log' rendering hint and a hard maxInputDigits=9 integer-only input clamp validated in the action zod schema.

Tie/precision edge cases (equal distances, exact hits, single answerer, zero answerers) must be locked in reducer tests before content scales: integers only, competition ranking, single answerer gets 100, zero answerers awards nothing and the round still advances on deadline.
Skill spread: a strong estimator can run away with the match. Mitigation: flat 100/50/25 payout + ×2 finale; watch round_completed/abandon analytics at 5% rollout before promoting.

Bilingual authoring must be split into single-locale packs (quizz-culture-ge-fr / -en) per synthesis §3.1 with FR/EN parity enforced as a pipeline lint — funFact punchlines must be natively funny in both languages, not machine-translated.

taglineFr: Chaque question désigne un coupable. Le pire pote gagne.
taglineEn: Every question points a finger. The worst friend wins.

phases.description: The round's designation card ('Qui serait capable de... / Who would...') appears on every phone simultaneously (no rotating card-drawer — see recommendations). Each player taps exactly ONE other player; the reducer rejects self-votes and re-votes are allowed until lock (last tap wins, tracer semantics). Early-resolve: the phase ends immediately when every rostered player has voted. Timeout behavior: at the deadline, missing votes (passive/disconnected players) are simply dropped — never blocks the room; if zero votes were cast the round awards nothing and advances.

Instant tally on every phone: who got how many fingers pointed at them. Every player holding the maximum tally (max >= 1) 'wins the shame card': +1 point, with a sticker animation framing it as a comedic WIN (brand: funny never cruel). Ties at max all score +1 (no revote — speed over precision). Auto-advances at the deadline to the next vote phase or to 'over'. No player input needed, so disconnects are irrelevant here.

Untimed terminal phase (phaseDurationMs = null). Final podium crowns 'Le Pire Pote / The Worst Mate' (highest cumulative shame-card count; final ties share the crown). Emits the gameOver effect with scores; lobby offers instant rematch with a fresh seed (the pack is shuffled at init so a rematch draws different cards).

contentItemShape: One pack item = one designation card: { id: string (stable, e.g. 'pp-014'), text: { fr: string, en: string } — the question, <= 140 chars, ALWAYS phrased to designate a person present in the room ('Qui...' / 'Who...'), 100% original writing (zero text reuse from 'Amis de merde'), transcreated not literally translated; spicy: 0 | 1 | 2 — item-level rating, an item may only ship in a pack whose tier >= its rating; tags?: string[] (e.g. 'soiree', 'argent', 'amour', 'absurde') for pack curation and anti-pile-on variety balancing. The bilingual file is the AUTHORING MASTER; the publish step splits it into single-locale packs (pires-potes-fr@N / pires-potes-en@N) per the platform pack-family convention (template-architecture §2.7), and the runtime pack data collapses to the VOTE module's existing { prompts: string[] } shape — the tracer module consumes it unchanged.

recommendations.question: Name (brief asks for 2-3 FR candidates, distinct from 'Amis de merde')
recommendations.recommendation: Candidates: 'Pires Potes', 'Potes Pourris', 'Sales Potes'. Pick 'Pires Potes' (EN display name 'Worst Mates').
recommendations.why: Matches the given game id pires-potes, alliterative and punchy on a Home tile, captures the 'worst friend wins' spirit, and is lexically distant from the 'Amis de merde' trademark (no shared word).

recommendations.question: Win condition: the original is 'first to 5 cards'; the platform wants short fixed TikTok-native sessions
recommendations.recommendation: v1 = fixed 7 rounds, highest score wins (pure VOTE@1 config, zero code). Later, add an optional targetScore param to VOTE@2 for a faithful 'first to 5' classic mode.
recommendations.why: First-to-N is unbounded (a 16-player room could run 20+ rounds); fixed 7 rounds = ~3 min session, fits the ad cadence and rematch loop, and the 'most shame cards wins' spirit is fully preserved. The param is a small additive reducer branch, not a launch blocker.

recommendations.question: Keep the physical game's rotating card-drawer turn?
recommendations.recommendation: Drop it. The card appears on all phones simultaneously every round; everyone votes at once.
recommendations.why: The drawer adds no decision in the original (they just read the card aloud), and a rotating 'active player' would let one disconnected player stall the room — violating the never-block rule. Simultaneous display is strictly faster and faithful to the spirit (the vote IS the game).

recommendations.question: Tie at max votes: revote or split?
recommendations.recommendation: All players tied at max get +1 (exact tracer behavior). No revote.
recommendations.why: Deterministic, zero extra phase, keeps rounds at ~27s. The drama is in WHO got designated, not in tiebreak bookkeeping; a revote phase would double round length for a rare case.

recommendations.question: Reveal style: instant or flip-one-by-one?
recommendations.recommendation: 'instant' for v1; A/B 'flip-one-by-one' later (the param is already specced in templateParamsSchema(VOTE) for Pass the Bloop).
recommendations.why: The original's fun is the immediate collective finger-point; instant keeps the round under 30s. Flip-one-by-one adds drama but costs ~5-8s/round — test it as a config flip once the VOTE revealStyle param lands.

recommendations.question: How to handle the original's edgy/dark tone vs Bloop's 'funny never cruel' + age gating?
recommendations.recommendation: Ship TWO sibling configs on the same template: 'pires-potes' (flagship, tone spicy, minAge 18, pack tiers 0+1) and 'pires-potes-soft' (tone classic, all ages, tier-0 cards only). Rewrite the humor angle: embarrassing and absurd, never humiliating identity/appearance/trauma.
recommendations.why: The schema already forces tone:'spicy' => minAge>=18 (template-architecture §2.1 refinement c), and sibling configs are the platform's standard tiering pattern — one KV edit each, no code. This keeps the original's bite for adult groups without shipping cruelty to minors.

recommendations.question: Param surface gap: voteMs/revealMs are in the module Config but not in templateParamsSchema(VOTE)
recommendations.recommendation: Grow templateParamsSchema(VOTE) with optional voteMs (5000-60000) and revealMs (3000-15000) overrides; pires-potes wants voteMs 20000 (vs tracer's 30000) and revealMs 7000 (vs 5000).
recommendations.why: Pure protocol-schema addition — the module already reads config.voteMs/revealMs, so no reducer change; until it lands, pires-potes runs fine on tracer defaults (rounds just 12s slower).

recommendations.question: Pack sizing and authoring path
recommendations.recommendation: Launch with >= 150 original cards per locale per tier (authored or AI-drafted OFFLINE through the §6 gate: schema + profanity scan + replay smoke + human curation), shuffled at init, totalRounds capped at pack size.
recommendations.why: 7 rounds/game with rematch loops burns cards fast; 150+ gives ~20 rematches before visible repeats. The AI pipeline is optional (hence needsOfflineAiPipeline=false — items carry no pre-computed values), but it is the cheap way to reach bilingual parity at volume; nothing AI ever runs at gameplay time.

risks: Copyright/trade-dress: the mechanic (vote-to-designate) is not protectable but card TEXTS and the name are. Hard rule: zero text reuse from 'Amis de merde'; run a similarity audit of the authored pack against the published deck before launch; keep name, logo and card visual design clearly distinct.

Pile-on/bullying: a designation game can dogpile one player all session. Mitigations: frame every designation as a comedic WIN (+1 'shame card' with celebratory sticker, scoreboard crowns the 'winner'), enforce pack variety via tags (absurd/flattering-negative mix, never identity/appearance/trauma angles), brand lint 'funny never cruel' in the §6 content gate, and the KV kill switch per pack.

Spicy compliance: the flagship config is tone:'spicy' so it MUST carry minAge>=18 and sit behind the self-attested age gate; store review may still flag dark-humor content — keep the soft sibling config as the default-surfaced tile for unverified-age devices.

Small-room dynamics: with 3 players (config floor; module floor is 2 but 2-player voting is trivial since you can only pick the other person) frequent max-ties mean multiple players score per round — score inflation is acceptable but the final crown ties more often; copy should celebrate co-winners.

Disconnect edge: if every player times out in a vote phase, zero votes => nobody scores and the round still advances (tracer's max>0 guard) — correct never-block behavior, but the UI must show a 'personne n'a voté / nobody voted' beat so it doesn't read as a bug.

Localization: humor must be transcreated, not translated — a literal EN rendering of a French 'photo dossier' joke falls flat; the bilingual authoring master needs native-quality passes per locale before the publish-time split into single-locale packs (synthesis §3.1 one-pack-one-locale convention).

taglineFr: Tout le monde a reçu le même mot… sauf un. Deux votes pour le démasquer.
taglineEn: Everyone got the same word… except one. Two votes to unmask them.

phases.description: Each phone privately shows ONLY the player's own secret item (word or theme) on a hold-to-peek card — no role is shown (revealRoleToSelf=false in decoy mode, so even the impostor doesn't know they're the odd one; classic Undercover paranoia). Theme label is public to all. Ends early when all alive&&connected players ack; deadline advances regardless, so a passive/disconnected phone never blocks.

Discussion period 1 (the brief's '2-3 min'): free face-to-face talk — players hint at their item without saying it, hunting for whose hints feel off. Phones show the theme, a countdown ring, and a 'Ready to vote' toggle; all alive&&connected ready → early vote. Deadline forces the vote. No typed text in this phase (talk is IRL), so zero moderation surface.

Simultaneous secret vote: tap the avatar you accuse. Ballots buffered in HIDDEN state (impostor-doc redaction rules verbatim: views carry hasVoted booleans + own myVote echo only, never the votes map). Self-vote inert, first vote locks, the impostor votes too (camouflage). Resolves when all alive&&connected voted, or at deadline with abstainers excluded.

Entered ONLY when vote 1 misses (the impostor is not the unique plurality target — tie or all-abstain also counts as a miss, favoring the impostor). Public beat: tally bars + the top accused is dramatically CLEARED ('Pas l'imposteur !'). Display-only, all actions inert; deadline auto-advances to discussion period 2.

Discussion period 2, shorter for escalating urgency (brief's 'une autre période 2-3 min', tuned down because the cleared-suspect info accelerates deduction). Same early-exit and deadline behavior as period 1.

Final vote, same rules as vote 1. Unique plurality on the impostor → caught; anything else (tie, wrong target, abstain-out) → the impostor wins, exactly per the brief ('si pas trouvé, l'imposteur gagne'). Always proceeds to finalReveal — never a third period.

Atomic full reveal: impostor identity, both secret items (majority + odd one), winning side banner, and exact points awarded. Deadline auto-advances to the next match's secretReveal (fresh item, fresh seeded impostor) or to standings + interstitial ad after matchesPerSession; phaseKey 'over' terminal.

contentItemShape: One odd-one-out content item (v1 = text only). Every player-visible string is a bilingual map { fr, en }; the offline pipeline splits items into per-locale R2 packs (<base>-fr / <base>-en) per the shell's pack-family convention, so init stays locale-free. Shape: { "id": string (stable slug), "mediaType": "text" (v2 roadmap: "image" | "audio", adding "media": { "majorityKey": string, "impostorKey": string } — R2 keys to PRE-RENDERED slightly-different assets, never generated at runtime), "theme": { fr, en } (PUBLIC label shown to the whole room), "majority": { fr, en } (HIDDEN item shown to all civilians), "impostor": { fr, en } (HIDDEN slightly-different item shown to the lone impostor — same theme, same abstractness, deliberately close), "closeness": "easy" | "medium" | "hard" (calibrated semantic distance: easy = far apart / impostor found fast, hard = nearly identical / impostor thrives; pre-scored offline), "spicyLevel": 0 | 1 | 2 (item-level gate; pack tone must match catalog tone) }. Authoring lint: pack must hold >= matchesPerSession items per locale with no duplicate ids; both items <= 3 tokens to fit the reveal card; all strings pass the obscenity scan at authoring time.

recommendations.question: Is this a new template, or the same family as the impostor/SECRET_ROLE design?
recommendations.recommendation: Same family — ship as a SECRET_ROLE game_config plus a small SECRET_ROLE@2 param extension: roundMode:'accusation' (no elimination; each vote asks 'is the unique plurality target the impostor?'), clueMode:'none' (skip the structured clue-turn loop entirely; discussion is IRL free talk), maxVoteRounds:2, revealRoleToSelf:false, impostorGuessEnabled:false. Do NOT create a NEW:ODD_ONE_OUT template.
recommendations.why: The brief is odd-one-out on shared content with hidden buffered votes — exactly impostor's state/redaction skeleton (roles, civilianWord/impostorWord, votes HIDDEN, RevealRecord). The template-architecture doc explicitly blesses small param riders on SECRET_ROLE (the NPC-Infiltrator secretKind precedent, §3.2 'new-params' effort class). A separate template would duplicate ~80% of the reducer and double the registry/catalog surface.

recommendations.question: The brief says '2-3 min' per period — what exact timers?
recommendations.recommendation: Default discussMs=120s for period 1 and discuss2Ms=90s for period 2, both within the brief's range via the existing SECRET_ROLE discussMs param cap (120s); allow catalog retune 90-180s. Both periods end early when all alive&&connected players tap 'Ready to vote'.
recommendations.why: Respects the brief's core pacing while staying TikTok-native: period 2 starts with the cleared-suspect info already on the table, so it needs less time, and a worst-case match stays under ~5 minutes (12+120+25+8+90+25+12 ≈ 292s).

recommendations.question: What exactly counts as 'l'imposteur est trouvé' at a vote?
recommendations.recommendation: Caught = the impostor is the UNIQUE plurality target of that vote. A tie at the top, a wrong unique target, or all-abstain = NOT caught (advances to period 2, or hands the impostor the win on vote 2). No revote sub-phase, no random tiebreak.
recommendations.why: Deterministic and pure (impostor doc §4.5 tie ruling reused verbatim); ties favoring the impostor is dramatic, keeps the reducer tiny, and lets the impostor's own ballot be a real sabotage tool.

recommendations.question: What is revealed after a missed vote 1?
recommendations.recommendation: Show the public tally and dramatically CLEAR the wrongly-accused top target ('X n'est pas l'imposteur !') in an 8s verdict beat — but never reveal who the impostor is until finalReveal. On a tie, show the tally with 'personne n'est démasqué' and clear nobody.
recommendations.why: Fuels period-2 deduction (the round needs new information to not be a rerun), and it's funny-never-cruel: the accused gets public vindication, not a roast. Risk of making vote 2 trivial in 4-5 player rooms is accepted and monitored (see risks).

recommendations.question: Does the impostor know they are the impostor? Does the room know the theme?
recommendations.recommendation: In the default decoy mode, nobody is told their role (revealRoleToSelf:false): every phone just shows 'your item'. The theme label is public to everyone. The impostor discovers they're odd only by listening.
recommendations.why: This is the brief's exact fantasy ('le dernier a un truc légèrement différent' — it never says he knows) and the strongest version of the paranoia: everyone simultaneously defends their item and doubts it. It also kills the 'impostor instantly overacts' failure mode.

recommendations.question: Keep the impostor-design guess window (caught impostor guesses the civilian word)?
recommendations.recommendation: OFF for v1 (impostorGuessEnabled:false). Ship it later as a config flip once the param exists in SECRET_ROLE@2.
recommendations.why: The brief specifies a clean two-vote structure; the guess window adds 20s + a text-input moderation path and dilutes the 'two votes, that's it' tension. Keeping v1 input-free (votes + taps only) means zero gameplay-text moderation surface.

recommendations.question: Image / video / music — content-pack strategy?
recommendations.recommendation: v1 ships text-only packs (word/theme pairs, human-curated with AI assist). v2 adds mediaType:'image' — pairs of PRE-RENDERED slightly-different images generated and QA'd by the offline AI pipeline, stored in R2, referenced by key; phones download both-eligible assets at match init and show only their own. Audio (10s royalty-free clips, each player listens on their own phone via the volume-warning pattern) is v3; video is last or never.
recommendations.why: Text proves the loop with zero licensing/sync risk. 'Slightly different' images are a perfect offline-AI job (generate variant + score the visual distance) and strictly forbidden at runtime by the determinism rule. Music/video carry licensing, file-size, and room-audio-chaos costs that don't change the mechanic.

recommendations.question: Exact scoring — who gets how many points when?
recommendations.recommendation: Per match: each civilian earns +1 per vote round in which their ballot targeted the impostor (max +2). Team catch bonus to EVERY civilian: +2 if caught on vote 1, +1 if caught on vote 2. Impostor: +2 for surviving vote 1 (kept even if caught on vote 2), +3 more for surviving vote 2 (impostor win = 5 total). If THE impostor disconnects past the grace window, the match ends immediately: civilians +1 each, impostor 0. Scores are match-local; the shell owns the session leaderboard and fires the interstitial only at the standings screen after matchesPerSession=3 (impostor doc §5.2 model).
recommendations.why: Rewards individual deduction (your ballot) AND the team outcome, gives the impostor a graded payoff for partial bluffing (so being caught on vote 2 still 'paid'), is computable in one pure pass at finalReveal, and never aliases live state in the gameOver effect.

recommendations.question: Player count?
recommendations.recommendation: Catalog-tighten to 4-16 (template floor is 3); sweet spot 5-10 in the tile copy.
recommendations.why: With no clue turns, a 3-player room degenerates: the impostor's single ballot forces ties too easily and discussion is a 1-v-1 accusation. game_config minPlayers is exactly the sanctioned tightener (template-architecture §2.6).

risks: Not literally zero-code: needs the SECRET_ROLE@2 param branch (roundMode:'accusation', clueMode:'none', maxVoteRounds, revealRoleToSelf, impostorGuessEnabled). Small and precedented (NPC-Infiltrator secretKind pattern, template-architecture §3.2), but it must land before this config can ship — schedule with the impostor/SECRET_ROLE build, not after.

120s+90s discussion phases are long versus platform norms (impostor uses 45s); shy or drunk-quiet groups risk dead air. Mitigate with the public theme card, a 'Ready to vote' early-exit, and on-screen nudge copy; watch round-abandon analytics at rolloutPct 5%.

Verdict info-leak: publicly clearing the wrongly-accused makes vote 2 near-trivial in 4-5 player rooms (one suspect eliminated from a tiny pool). If analytics show vote-2 catch rate >> design target (~55-65%), fall back to tally-only verdict (no explicit clearing) via a config param.

Pair-closeness calibration is the whole game: too close and the impostor is unfindable (frustration), too far and round 1 is instant (boring). Requires the offline AI pipeline to score semantic distance per pair plus human playtest of every 'hard' item before enabled:true (AI gate stages 2 and 5).

Ties structurally favor the impostor and the impostor votes too — a coordinated impostor can engineer top-ties. Accepted as a feature (deterministic, dramatic), but cap monitoring: if impostor win rate > ~50% at 6+ players, revisit the tie-counts-as-miss ruling.

Impostor disconnect mid-match invalidates the round; the reducer must end the match on grace expiry (civilians +1 consolation) using the alive&&connected resolution rule — an unhandled impostor-left path would leave the room hunting a ghost for 4 minutes.

v2+ media packs: image generation/QA cost, R2 asset weight on party Wi-Fi, music licensing, and multi-phone audio chaos in one room. None block v1 (text-only), but the catalog entry must not promise media in the tile copy until packs exist.

Bilingual authoring drift: {fr,en} item pairs must stay semantically parallel (same closeness in both locales) or FR and EN rooms play different difficulty curves; the offline pipeline should score closeness per locale, not once.

taglineFr: Deux ambiances : la soirée entre potes, ou le tête-à-tête qui chauffe.
taglineEn: Two vibes: party night with the crew, or date night that heats up.

phases.description: Active player (seeded rotation, disconnected seats skipped) picks Truth or Dare via big chips; everyone else sees the waiting card + rotation rail. Timeout: deterministic seeded auto-pick (createRng(seed+'|coin|'+turnSeq)). phaseKey = `choose:${turnSeq}` where turnSeq is a global monotonic per-turn counter (never the round number — uniqueness rule from the ToD design §2).

The drawn prompt (seeded no-repeat deck per `${choice}:${intensity}`, fall-down on tier exhaustion) is shown to the WHOLE room; the active player performs the dare / answers the truth out loud IRL, then taps Done or Chickened, or burns a Pass (if passesLeft > 0). Pass and self-declared Chicken skip the verdict and go straight to score. Timeout: treated as chickened, no pass spent — a passive player never blocks the room. phaseKey = `prompt:${turnSeq}`.

Reached ONLY after a 'Done' claim. Every present player except the active one votes done/chickened (enum vote, no free text). Ends early when all eligible voters have voted; timeout tallies whatever votes are in. Resolution: 0 votes cast → done (benefit of the doubt); else done iff doneCount/castVotes >= verdictThreshold (0.5, ties → done). If the eligible set is empty at entry (e.g. 2-player room, partner disconnected) resolve immediately as done. Individual votes are HIDDEN (counts only) until score. phaseKey = `verdict:${turnSeq}`.

Reveal: DONE/CHICKENED/PASSED stamp, public tally bar, +points burst, mini-leaderboard, 'next up' banner. No actions accepted; deadline advances to the next present player's choose, or to over after the final lap. EXACT SCORING (active player only; voters never score): done+truth = 10 pts; done+dare = 15 pts (10 donePoints + 5 dareBonus); passed = 3 pts (passPoints, one pass consumed); chickened (declared, timed out, voted down, or active left mid-turn) = 0 pts. One ROUND = one full lap of the rotation (~70s × players); roundsDefault counts laps. Lap wrap emits analytics 'round_completed' = the interstitial ad boundary (never mid-lap, never after the final lap). phaseKey = `score:${turnSeq}`.

Untimed terminal phase (phaseDurationMs = null, phaseKey = 'over'). Final ranked leaderboard + podium; gameOver effect carries final scores. Also reached early on total content-pool exhaustion (graceful degrade per ToD design §4).

contentItemShape: AUTHORING entry shape (bilingual at authoring; the build pipeline splits it into single-locale R2 packs per cross-game-synthesis §3.1/§3.3 pack-family rule — tod2-fun-fr / tod2-fun-en / tod2-lover-fr / tod2-lover-en, each entry keeping only its locale's text): { id: string — stable unique no-repeat key, format '<pack>-<t|d>-<tier>-<nnn>' (e.g. 'lov-d-spicy-009'); choice: 'truth' | 'dare'; intensity: 'soft' | 'party' | 'spicy' — the template's draw tier (fun pack ships soft+party only, lover pack ships party+spicy only); spicy: 0 | 1 | 2 — catalog rating of THIS entry (fun entries 0-1, lover entries 1-2; must never exceed the pack ceiling — lint in the AI gate); minAge: 13 | 16 | 18 — every intensity:'spicy' entry MUST be 18 (ToD design §6 hard rule); text: { fr: string, en: string } — the prompt verbatim, second person, <= 280 chars, pre-moderated (obscenity-scanned at authoring, never at runtime), judgeable by the room (the verdict phase needs a visible/audible outcome); props?: boolean — needs a phone/object; tags?: string[] — curation metadata ('funny','physical','deep','couple','spicy'); every lover-pack entry carries 'couple'. Runtime shape is the existing TodPromptEntry — no template or reducer change.

text.fr: Quel est le truc le plus absurde que tu aies cherché sur Google cette semaine ?
text.en: What's the most ridiculous thing you googled this week?

text.fr: Laisse la personne à ta droite écrire un message à qui elle veut depuis ton téléphone — tu as 3 secondes pour le relire avant l'envoi.
text.en: Let the person on your right text anyone they want from your phone — you get 3 seconds to read it before it sends.

text.fr: Raconte le moment exact où tu as su que tu craquais pour ton/ta partenaire — avec tous les détails gênants.
text.en: Describe the exact moment you knew you were falling for your partner — embarrassing details included.

recommendations.question: Is truth-or-dare-2 a new game, a new template, or pack variants?
recommendations.recommendation: CONFIRMED: pack variants. Zero new code — two sibling game_config entries on the existing TRUTH_DARE template (docs/designs/2026-06-10-game-truth-or-dare-design.md), shipped via Cadence B only (R2 packs + KV catalog edit, no deploy). The top-level fields of this output describe the FUN mainline config; the LOVER sibling is fully specified below.
recommendations.why: Every mechanic the brief needs already exists in the designed template: turn rotation, Truth/Dare choice, group verdict, pass economy, intensity tiers, deck-draw-without-repeat. The brief's 'deux ambiances' are exactly the content/params axis the template was parameterized for (template-architecture §2.4 TRUTH_DARE params, §3.2 row 6 'config-only per variant').

recommendations.question: One Home tile with an ambiance picker, or two tiles?
recommendations.recommendation: Two sibling configs/tiles: `truth-or-dare-fun-2026` (tone:'classic', minAge:13, players 2-16, theme bubblegum/fire, params {totalRounds:3, passesPerPlayer:2, allowedIntensities:['soft','party'], verdictThreshold:0.5}) and `truth-or-dare-lover-2026` (tone:'spicy', minAge:18, players 2-8, theme raw #E0356B/heart, badge NEW, params {totalRounds:4, passesPerPlayer:3, allowedIntensities:['party','spicy'], verdictThreshold:0.5}).
recommendations.why: Age-gating is per-config (gameConfigSchema refinement (c): spicy tone forces minAge>=18) and catalog params are catalog-fixed by default (template-architecture §7 Q4). A single tile cannot be simultaneously family-safe and 18+; an in-lobby ambiance toggle would put 18+ content one tap behind a family tile.

recommendations.question: Lover variant player range — couples only at 2, or more?
recommendations.recommendation: minPlayers 2, maxPlayers 8 (1 to 4 couples), designed-for and marketed at 2. Lobby copy: 'en couple(s) uniquement'.
recommendations.why: The template floor is already 2 and the 2-player verdict edge (partner alone judges, abstain→done) is fully specced (ToD design §4 edge counts). Prompts say 'ton/ta partenaire' — the phone never needs the pairing, the room knows it. Capping at 8 keeps verdicts intimate and avoids 16-player lover rooms that would misfire socially.

recommendations.question: How does the brief's spicy 0-1 / 1-2 mapping land on the template's soft/party/spicy tiers?
recommendations.recommendation: Fun pack: soft tier = spicy 0, party tier = spicy 1; it contains NO spicy-tier entries at all. Lover pack: party tier = spicy 1 (tender/flirty), spicy tier = spicy 2 (18+, suggestive); it contains no soft tier. Configs gate accordingly: fun allowedIntensities ['soft','party']; lover ['party','spicy'] behind tone:'spicy' + minAge 18 + the server spicy feature flag (ToD design §6).
recommendations.why: Reuses the template's existing 3-tier system with zero reducer change, and keeping 18+ entries physically out of the fun pack removes the dormant-spicy-tier store-compliance ambiguity that tod-classic carries (a pack may contain spicy; here the fun pack simply doesn't).

recommendations.question: Lover pass economy and scoring — same as fun?
recommendations.recommendation: passesPerPlayer: 3 in lover (vs 2 in fun); all scoring identical and NOT config-exposed (template DEFAULT_CONFIG): done+truth 10, done+dare 15 (10+5 dareBonus), passed 3, chickened 0, voters unscored, verdictThreshold 0.5 ties→done.
recommendations.why: Consent-forward design: declining an intimate dare must always feel cheap, so the lover skip economy gets a higher floor (ToD design §9 Q4 flags pass tuning as the playtest knob). Scoring knobs are deliberately absent from templateParamsSchema(TRUTH_DARE) (template-architecture §2.4), so both variants ride the template defaults — no schema change.

recommendations.question: How far does the lover 18+ (spicy 2) content ceiling go?
recommendations.recommendation: Suggestive, partner-directed, consent-forward; NEVER explicit/graphic, never degrading or coercive, no contact with non-partners, everything skippable via pass. Authoring rubric: every dare must have a room-visible, judgeable outcome (the verdict phase) without the explicit part happening in front of the room — the lov-d-spicy-009 sample (whisper + straight face, room judges the face) is the canonical pattern.
recommendations.why: Brand Book 'funny never cruel' + Apple 1.1 / Google sexual-content tiers (ToD design §6, §9 Q2). The verdict mechanic structurally requires judgeable-in-room outcomes, which conveniently caps explicitness.

recommendations.question: Tier pacing in lover rooms — the template plays the highest allowed tier first (ToD design §4), so lover rooms open straight at spicy-2. Acceptable?
recommendations.recommendation: Ship v1 as-is (spicy-first with fall-down to party on exhaustion). If playtests confirm the abrupt opening, the fix is a small TRUTH_DARE@2 param `tierProgression: 'fixed-highest' | 'escalate'` (round index maps to ascending tiers: lap 1 party, laps 2+ spicy) — a tiny reducer branch, explicitly NOT a launch blocker. Do not fake escalation with two stacked configs.
recommendations.why: Per-turn/per-round tier selection is exactly ToD design §9 Q1's deferred alternative; respecting the v1 room-fixed ruling keeps this release pure Cadence B. The brief's 'ambiance' wording implies pacing matters, so the @2 param is pre-scoped here.

recommendations.question: Pack sizing and authoring volume?
recommendations.recommendation: Apply the synthesis §3.5 lint: fun pack >= 48 entries per (choice, tier) (16 players x 3 rounds) = >= 192 per locale; lover pack >= 32 per (choice, tier) (8 players x 4 rounds) = >= 128 per locale. With ~20% headroom: ~460 fun + ~310 lover entries total across FR+EN. needsOfflineAiPipeline is FALSE (no runtime AI, no pre-computed values), but AI-ASSISTED drafting of this volume is recommended — it is optional and must pass the full template-architecture §6 gate (schema + obscenity scan + replay smoke + human FR/EN naturalness sign-off) before enabled:true, rolloutPct 5 then 100.
recommendations.why: ~770 bilingual entries is the real cost of this 'zero-code' game; under-sizing triggers tier fall-down or early game end at max rooms (ToD design §4). The §6 gate already exists for exactly this workflow — innuendo-heavy lover content especially needs the human naturalness pass (machine-translated flirting reads as creepy).

risks: Age gate is self-attested on an anonymous platform: minors can lie into the 18+ lover config. Mitigations: server/region feature flag default-OFF for spicy (ToD design §6), non-explicit content ceiling, per-prompt report path keyed by prompt.id, KV pack/config kill switch — but residual risk needs product+legal sign-off before lover ever flips enabled:true (ToD design §9 Q2 is still an open call).

Store compliance (Apple 1.1 / Google sexual-content tiers): the lover tile existing at all in a 4+/Everyone-rated app may force a rating change; verify the storefront rating strategy before building the packs, not after.

Lover config started in a non-couple room: 'ton/ta partenaire' prompts misfire socially for a third wheel. Mitigated only softly (lobby copy, 2-8 cap, pass economy) — the engine has no pairing concept and adding one would be new code; accept and monitor abandon analytics.

2-player verdict feel: the partner alone judges (and could grief). ToD design §9 Q3/Q6 left this open; acceptable for flirty lover stakes but must be playtested — fallback is advisory-only verdicts at 2 players, which would be a template param change.
Highest-tier-first pacing means lover rooms open at spicy-2 with no warm-up; flagged with a pre-scoped TRUTH_DARE@2 'escalate' param if playtests confirm (see recommendations).

Content volume (~770 bilingual entries) is the hidden critical path of this 'zero-code' game; AI-drafted entries that skip the human FR/EN naturalness gate will read as machine-mush, worst in the lover register.

Authoring drift: fun-pack 'party' entries creeping into spicy-2 territory. Enforce per-entry spicy rating <= pack ceiling as a hard lint in the §6 validation gate (entry.spicy in {0,1} for fun, {1,2} for lover; intensity:'spicy' implies minAge 18).

Single top-level spicyLevel cannot represent both variants: this output's spicyLevel=1 describes the FUN mainline config only; the LOVER sibling config is spicyLevel 2 / tone:'spicy' / minAge 18 — any downstream catalog tooling must take the per-config values from recommendations, not the umbrella number.

taglineFr: Un chiffre secret en tête. À vous de lire dans ses pensées.
taglineEn: They've got a secret number in mind. Read them like a book.

phases.description: The round's speaker (rotates each round via nextActiveSeat) privately sees the secret target — an integer 1-10 (scale10 mode) or 0-100 (wheel100 mode) — plus the round's prompt and scale anchors. Everyone else sees only the prompt and anchors. Speaker taps Ready to advance early; deadline auto-advances. Timeout/disconnect: if the speaker is gone, deadline still fires; speaker playerLeft voids the round immediately (skip to a voided reveal, no points).

The in-room beat, fully verbal: the speaker answers the prompt (or fields the group's questions) calibrated to their secret number — e.g. describes a dish worth exactly a 7/10. Phones show the scale; only the speaker's phone keeps the secret. Speaker may tap 'Open the votes' to end early (speakerCanEndTalk). Deadline always advances; a silent or disconnected speaker can never block (speaker playerLeft here also voids the round).

All connected non-speakers privately set a dial/slider to their guess (integer, clamped to the mode's domain). Hidden buffer with owner-echo only (myGuess = guesses[viewer] ?? null); others see hasGuessed booleans. Advances early when allActed(connected non-speakers, guesses); at deadline, missing guesses simply score 0 — a passive or disconnected player never blocks. A guesser leaving re-checks allActed (if they were the last awaited, resolve immediately). Overwrites allowed until resolve.

Atomic promotion: the target plus every guess is plotted on the dial. Band points awarded to each guesser by distance; the speaker scores the band of the lower-median guess distance (rewards calibrating the whole room). Emits analytics round_revealed on entry and round_completed at the reveal→next boundary (the shell's ad cue fires off the phaseKey transition, not the analytics). Deadline rotates the speaker and starts the next round's target phase, or ends the game with gameOver(cloned scores) after totalRounds.

contentItemShape: Authoring-source item (bilingual; the pack build pipeline splits it into single-locale runtime packs `la-note-fr` / `la-note-en` per synthesis §3.1): { id: string; kind: 'scale10' | 'wheel100'; prompt: { fr: string, en: string } — the instruction the speaker performs out loud, calibrated to the secret number; low: { fr, en } — anchor label for 1 / the left end of the wheel; high: { fr, en } — anchor label for 10 / the right end; tags?: string[]; intensity?: 'classic' | 'spicy' (spicy items only ship in spicy packs, tone:'spicy' + minAge>=18). RULE: one pack contains ONE kind only and the game_config's params.mode must match it (validated by the authoring lint / AI gate — init never filters, per synthesis §3.3). Runtime ContentPack.data = { locale: 'fr'|'en', tone?: 'classic'|'spicy', items: ScaleItem[] } with single-locale strings. Targets are NOT in the pack — they are drawn at init from the seeded RNG (pure math scoring, no pre-computed answer needed).
