newTemplateSpec:
TEMPLATE: SCALE_GUESS — new GameModule package `packages/games/scale-guess/` (id 'scale-guess', version 1, minPlayers 3, maxPlayers 16). Fits GameModule<S,A,V,C> with ZERO contract amendments: uses the approved phaseKey (synthesis A1) and the shared kit (emptyPlayerMap, Presence/connectedPlayers, allActed, nextActiveSeat, gameOver helper). No new event or effect types. No gameplay text — the talk beat is verbal in the room — so NO moderation surface (lower-risk than INPUT_GUESS).

CONFIG (DEFAULT_CONFIG; catalog params are a strict partial): { mode: 'scale10'|'wheel100' (REQUIRED, mode-selecting like INPUT_GUESS.mode), totalRounds: 8, targetReadMs: 8000, talkMs: 45000, guessMs: 20000, revealMs: 8000, speakerCanEndTalk: true }. Domain: scale10 → integers 1..10; wheel100 → integers 0..100 (slider with snap ticks every 5; no float angles — deterministic state/replay).
templateParamsSchema addition (packages/protocol): z.object({ mode: z.enum(['scale10','wheel100']), totalRounds: z.number().int().min(1).max(16).optional(), targetReadMs: z.number().int().min(3000).max(15000).optional(), talkMs: z.number().int().min(20000).max(120000).optional(), guessMs: z.number().int().min(10000).max(45000).optional(), revealMs: z.number().int().min(4000).max(15000).optional(), speakerCanEndTalk: z.boolean().optional() }).strict().

CONTENT: ContentPack<{ locale: 'fr'|'en'; tone?: 'classic'|'spicy'; items: ScaleItem[] }>; ScaleItem = { id, kind, prompt, low, high, tags? } (single-locale at runtime; bilingual authoring source split by the pack build). One pack = one kind; config.mode must equal the pack kind (authoring lint / AI gate; init never filters per synthesis §3.3). Sizing lint: items.length >= totalRounds, recommend >= 24.

STATE S: { config; players: PlayerId[]; turnOrder: PlayerId[] /* seeded shuffle */; connected: Presence; round: number; phase: 'target'|'talk'|'guess'|'reveal'|'over'; speakerIndex: number; items: ScaleItem[] /* seeded shuffle; items[round] current */; targets: number[] /* HIDDEN — pre-drawn for ALL rounds at init from createRng(seed), so determinism never depends on event order */; guesses: Record<PlayerId, number> /* HIDDEN buffer */; voided: boolean; scores: Record<PlayerId, number> }. init: totalRounds = min(config.totalRounds, items.length); scores all 0; phase 'target', round 0, speakerIndex 0.

ACTIONS A: { kind:'ready' } (speaker only, target phase → talk early) | { kind:'openVotes' } (speaker only, talk phase, iff speakerCanEndTalk → guess early) | { kind:'guess', value:number } (non-speaker only, guess phase; non-integer or out-of-domain → REJECT by returning the SAME state reference; overwrites allowed until resolve, hot-seat §4.1 convention; after each accepted write, if allActed(connectedPlayers minus speaker, guesses) → resolveReveal early). Any other (sender, phase) combo → same-reference reject (shell no-op contract).

REDUCE (phase × event): target: ready|deadline → talk. talk: openVotes|deadline → guess. guess: deadline → resolveReveal with submitted guesses only. reveal: deadline → round+1; if round >= totalRounds → phase 'over' + gameOver(Object.assign(emptyPlayerMap(), scores)); else nextActiveSeat(turnOrder, speakerIndex, connected), guesses = emptyPlayerMap(), voided=false, phase 'target'. playerLeft: flip connected only (roster/scores untouched, seat greyed); if leaver is the CURRENT SPEAKER during target or talk → void round: jump to reveal with voided=true, zero points, analytics 'round_skipped'; during guess → round resolves normally (target fixed, talk happened); if leaver is a guesser during guess → re-check allActed and resolve immediately if they were last awaited. playerRejoined: flip connected; a rejoined guesser in guess phase is expected again. over: absolute no-op.

SCORING (exact): d = |guess − targets[round]|. Guesser bands — scale10: d=0→4 pts, d=1→2, d=2→1, d>=3→0. wheel100: d<=5→4, d<=10→3, d<=20→2, d<=33→1, d>33→0. Speaker: D = ascending sorted distances of SUBMITTED guesses; if D empty or voided → 0; else speaker pts = band(D[floor((D.length−1)/2)]) (lower median) through the same table. Ties: every guesser in the best band scores it — 'closest wins' means all closest win (funny never cruel). Max 4 pts/round for everyone; session leaderboard stays placement-based (synthesis §1.7).

VIEW V (per-viewer redaction): target/talk → PUBLIC { phase, round, totalRounds, item{prompt,low,high}, speakerId, scores, connected }; speaker view ADDS { target }. guess → public + { hasGuessed: Record<PlayerId, boolean> }, per-viewer myGuess = guesses[viewer] ?? null (owner echo only), speaker keeps target. reveal → PUBLIC { target, plottedGuesses, gained, voided, scores } (atomic promotion). over → { phase:'over', scores }. Unknown/spectator viewer → public projection, never target, never buffer.
phaseKey: `${phase}:r${round}` ('target:r0' … 'reveal:r7'), terminal 'over'. One speaker per round so the round index alone is unique per phase instance (synthesis §1.6). The key NEVER embeds the target. phaseDurationMs: target→targetReadMs, talk→talkMs, guess→guessMs, reveal→revealMs, over→null.

EFFECTS: analytics 'round_revealed' on reveal entry; 'round_completed' at the reveal→next boundary (ad interstitial fires off the phaseKey transition per synthesis §5.4 — analytics is PostHog-only); 'round_skipped' on a voided round; gameOver with cloned scores (never aliasing live state).

TESTS (load-bearing): redaction audit — String(targets[round]) absent from every non-speaker/spectator view JSON during target/talk/guess (leakedSecrets-style; targets are numbers, audit the stringified speaker-only field); guesses never leak cross-player pre-reveal; replay determinism with pinned { packId, version } + seed; speaker-leave-voids-round in target/talk; deadline-resolves-partial-guesses; out-of-domain guess returns same reference; gameOver scores don't alias state.

CATALOG (two game_configs, both variants of the brief, zero extra code beyond the template): (1) { id:'jeu-de-la-note', template:'SCALE_GUESS', templateVersion:{min:1,max:1}, params:{ mode:'scale10', totalRounds:8, targetReadMs:8000, talkMs:45000, guessMs:20000, revealMs:8000, speakerCanEndTalk:true }, contentPackRef:{ packId:'la-note', version:1 }, theme:{ color:'sunbeam', icon:'gauge', badge:'NEW' }, tone:'classic', minAge:0, locales:['fr','en'], minPlayers:3 }. (2) { id:'la-roue', params:{ mode:'wheel100', talkMs:60000 }, contentPackRef:{ packId:'la-roue', version:1 }, theme:{ color:'aqua', icon:'shuffle' } } — the brief's wheel variant as a pure config rider. Build slot: after rank-friends and hot-seat land (it reuses rank-friends' simultaneous hidden buffer + hot-seat's seat rotation); it can ship before INPUT_GUESS since it has no text-moderation surface.

recommendations.question: The brief gives two variants (secret number/wheel angle with Q&A, and labeled 1-10 scale where the speaker answers to match the number) — which mechanic ships?
recommendations.recommendation: One SCALE_GUESS template with a params.mode discriminant ('scale10' | 'wheel100'); ship the 'jeu-de-la-note' scale10 config first, the 'la-roue' wheel100 config second.
recommendations.why: Both variants share the identical skeleton (single-holder secret target → verbal calibration → simultaneous hidden numeric guess → closeness reveal); only the domain and reveal rendering differ — exactly the 'modes within one template' pattern the architecture doc uses for INPUT_GUESS. scale10 with labeled anchors is the most legible on first play; the wheel then rides for free as a config.

recommendations.question: How do 'les autres joueurs lui posent des questions' work without phones collecting text or a passive player blocking the room?
recommendations.recommendation: A single timer-boxed talk phase (45s default), fully verbal in the room; the speaker may tap 'Open the votes' to end early; the deadline always advances.
recommendations.why: Phones stay controllers/secret-keepers (platform rule) — no typed gameplay text means no moderation surface and no stall vector; the timer + early-end keeps rounds TikTok-short (~81s) and a disconnected speaker voids the round instead of freezing it.

recommendations.question: 'Le plus proche gagne' — what is the exact scoring?
recommendations.recommendation: Band scoring for guessers (scale10: exact=4, ±1=2, ±2=1, else 0; wheel100: d≤5=4, ≤10=3, ≤20=2, ≤33=1, else 0) and the speaker scores the band of the lower-median guess distance (0 if no guesses or round voided).
recommendations.why: All closest guessers score the top band — ties produce shared wins, never a cruel single loser; the median rewards the speaker for calibrating the WHOLE room rather than one lucky friend; it is pure deterministic integer math (no judge, no AI at runtime) and capped at 4/round for everyone, keeping scores comparable.

recommendations.question: Can this reuse HOT_SEAT (or INPUT_GUESS) instead of new code?
recommendations.recommendation: No — propose NEW:SCALE_GUESS, then both brief variants plus all future packs are config-only.
recommendations.why: HOT_SEAT's hidden answer is strictly binary 0|1 with match-points (hot-seat doc §3-§4); INPUT_GUESS is free-text/peer-tap. A numeric dial domain, a per-round secret held by ONE player, and closeness-band scoring require a different reducer — per the template-architecture honesty rule that's a Cadence A template build (~1-2 weeks), after which the wheel config and every new pack ship with no deploy (Cadence B).

recommendations.question: Does the speaker also guess or score on their own round, and do they type their answer?
recommendations.recommendation: The speaker never guesses (excluded from the buffer and from allActed) and never types — their phone only holds the secret; they score via the median band.
recommendations.why: Self-guessing is degenerate (they know the target); typing would create a text-moderation surface and kill the in-room performance, which is the actual fun.

recommendations.question: Is the wheel a continuous angle or discrete?
recommendations.recommendation: Integer 0..100 slider rendered as a dial, with snap ticks every 5.
recommendations.why: Integers keep state JSON-safe and replay-deterministic, distances exactly comparable, and the reveal plot readable on a phone screen; the dial rendering still delivers the 'roue' fantasy from the brief.

risks: This is a NEW template (Cadence A): reducer + dial/slider client component + registry entries + a wrangler/eas deploy — not a config-only ship; budget ~1-2 weeks like the other designed templates.

The secret target is the load-bearing redaction surface: it must appear ONLY in the speaker's view before reveal, never in phaseKey, analytics props, or spectator views — needs a leakedSecrets-style audit test on the stringified target from day one.
Speaker disconnect mid-round must void/skip the round immediately (voided reveal + round_skipped) or the room stalls waiting on a ghost; the playerLeft branches need dedicated tests.
Shy or silent rooms can make the verbal talk phase drag — mitigated by the 45s cap and speaker early-end, but watch round-abandon analytics at rolloutPct 5 before promoting to 100.
At minPlayers=3 there are only 2 guessers, so the lower-median speaker score is coarse (it equals the better guess); acceptable but verify the feel in playtest before lowering timers further.

Pack quality is the real difficulty knob: anchors must be genuinely graduated or all guesses cluster mid-scale and bands flatten; enforce the sizing lint (items >= totalRounds, recommend >= 24) and the AI-gate playtest rubric.

Bilingual authoring items must be split into single-locale runtime packs (la-note-fr / la-note-en) by the build pipeline per synthesis §3.1 — shipping a mixed-language pack violates the loader convention.
Dial precision on small screens (wheel100): without snap ticks and haptics, fat-finger error masquerades as bad reads; UX must make the ±5 bullseye band physically reachable.

taglineFr: Tu as sa réponse. Mais c'était quoi la question ?
taglineEn: You've got their answer. But what was the question?

phases.description: The spotlight player (the 'mystery player', rotating through a seeded seatOrder like HOT_SEAT) privately sees the secret question + 3-4 answer options and picks their honest answer. Everyone else sees only 'X is answering a secret question...' (no question, no options — zero leak). Early exit: answer submitted -> immediately enter guess:h0. Timeout/answerer-left: round is VOIDED (voidRound=true) -> jump to reveal showing 'no answer — round void', 0 points, advance. A passive answerer never blocks the room.

Tier 0 (no hint, max points). All players now see the chosen ANSWER text + a seeded-shuffled list of 5 candidate questions (1 real + 4 decoys). Guessers lock ONE candidate (first-write-wins; the lock records tier=0 worth 300 pts if correct). View shows locked: Record<PlayerId,boolean> only — never anyone's pick. Early exit: all connected guessers locked -> reveal. Deadline -> hint 1 revealed, enter h1 (phaseKey change re-arms the alarm).

Tier 1: pre-authored hint #1 (from the content pack) is now public to everyone. Unlocked guessers may still lock (tier=1, 200 pts if correct). Early exit: all locked -> reveal. Deadline -> hint 2 revealed, enter h2.

Tier 2 (last chance): hint #2 public. Locks here are worth 100 pts if correct. Early exit: all locked -> reveal. Deadline -> reveal regardless (no-guess players simply score 0 — abstention is free, never blocking).

Atomic promotion: real question highlighted among the candidates, every guesser's pick + lock tier flips public, +points count-up (gained deltas), mystery player's read-bonus shown. Emits analytics round_revealed. Deadline -> next round's answer, or scoreboard if due/last round.

Running-totals beat inserted every scoreboardEvery=2 rounds and always once before over — this is the interstitial ad slot (shell fires AdMob off the phaseKey transition to scoreboard:*, subject to remote-config caps). Deadline -> next round or over.
Terminal, untimed (phaseDurationMs=null). gameOver effect with cloned final scores; shell awards session XP by placement (synthesis §1.7), reducer is a no-op.

contentItemShape: One pack item = { id: string (stable, e.g. "q_mirror"); question: {fr,en} — the secret real question (max 140 chars); answers: Array<{fr,en}> of 3-4 honest-answer options the mystery player picks from — each option MUST read as a plausible answer to the real question AND to every decoy (this cross-plausibility is the whole game and the offline-AI scoring target); decoys: Array<{fr,en}> of exactly decoyCount (4) fake questions, same register/length as the real one; hints: Array<{fr,en}> of exactly hintTiers-1 (2) progressive hints about the real question, ordered least->most revealing, never quoting the question verbatim; tags: string[] (theme/curation); spicy?: 0|1|2 (pack-level tone still rules catalog gating). Pack envelope: { locale-parallel FR+EN inline per item as shown (the shell serves the room-locale strings; both locales mandatory per item), version: int, items: Item[] }. Sizing lint: >= totalRounds(6) drawable items minimum, 40+ recommended. At init the module seed-shuffles items, takes totalRounds, and per item seed-shuffles [real + decoys] into a candidates array storing realIndex as HIDDEN state.

TEMPLATE: REVERSE_GUESS — rotating-spotlight secret-question MCQ with progressive pre-authored hints and tier-decaying scoring. Implements GameModule<RGState, RGAction, RGView, RGContent> on the existing contract (zero amendments: phaseKey A1 + the §1 kit cover everything). minPlayers 3 (1 answerer + 2 guessers minimum for social spread), maxPlayers 16.

STATE (JSON-safe, null-proto maps via emptyPlayerMap):
RGConfig { totalRounds:6; answerMs:20000; hintTiers:3; hintIntervalMs:20000; revealMs:8000; scoreboardMs:6000; scoreboardEvery:2; decoyCount:4; tierPoints:[300,200,100]; readerPointsPerCorrectGuess:75 }.
RGState {
  config; players: PlayerId[]; seatOrder: PlayerId[] (shuffle(createRng(seed), players));
  rounds: Array<{ itemId; answerOptions: string[]; candidates: string[] /* seeded shuffle of [realQuestion, ...decoys], PUBLIC from guess phase */; realIndex: number /* HIDDEN until reveal */; hints: string[] /* public once their tier opens */ }> — built at init: shuffle items, take min(totalRounds, items.length), per-round seeded candidate shuffle; locale strings pre-resolved by the shell-selected pack (init is locale-free per synthesis §3.3);
  round; totalRounds; seatIndex; phase: 'answer'|'guess'|'reveal'|'scoreboard'|'over'; hintTier: number; sinceScoreboard;
  chosenAnswer: number|null  // HIDDEN during 'answer' (only the answerer's own echo); PUBLIC from 'guess';
  guesses: Record<PlayerId, { candidateIndex:number; tier:number }>  // HIDDEN buffer until reveal; owner-echo only;
  voidRound: boolean; scores: Record<PlayerId, number>; connected: Presence (kit §1.2);
}

ACTIONS (zod at DO boundary; no free text anywhere — zero moderation surface):
RGAction = { kind:'answer'; answerIndex:number } | { kind:'guess'; candidateIndex:number }.

REDUCE TABLE (reject = same state reference, per contract):
- answer + action(answer) from currentSeat (seatOrder[seatIndex]) with valid index -> set chosenAnswer, phase='guess', hintTier=0. From anyone else, or invalid index: no-op.
- answer + deadline, OR playerLeft(answerer) while unanswered -> voidRound=true, phase='reveal' (reveal renders 'no answer — round void', all gained=0). Never blocks.
- guess + action(guess) from a connected non-answerer NOT already in guesses (first-write-wins lock) with valid candidateIndex -> record {candidateIndex, tier: hintTier}. If allActed(expected = connectedPlayers minus answerer, guesses) -> resolveReveal early. Duplicate/answerer/out-of-range: no-op.
- guess + deadline -> if hintTier+1 < hintTiers: hintTier++ (hint becomes public; phaseKey changes so the shell re-arms hintIntervalMs); else resolveReveal.
- resolveReveal: for each guesser g with guesses[g].candidateIndex === realIndex: gained[g] = tierPoints[guesses[g].tier]; answerer gained = correctCount * readerPointsPerCorrectGuess (0 if voidRound). scores += gained. Emits analytics round_revealed {round, correct, tierHistogram, voided}; phase='reveal'. Guesses stay in state through reveal (tracer pattern — view recomputes), cleared on startNextRound.
- reveal + deadline -> advance: last round OR sinceScoreboard<=0 -> phase='scoreboard' (emit analytics round_completed — the spec §8.6 lap boundary), else startNextRound.
- scoreboard + deadline -> round+1 >= totalRounds ? gameOver (cloned scores) : startNextRound (round++, seatIndex = nextActiveSeat(seatOrder, seatIndex, connected), phase='answer', guesses cleared, chosenAnswer=null, voidRound=false, sinceScoreboard rotated).
- playerLeft: connected=false; if phase='guess' re-check allActed (their absence may complete the round); if they are the answerer in 'answer', void (above); mid-'guess' answerer leave is harmless (chosenAnswer already public). playerRejoined: connected=true (can only ADD an expected actor — no resolve check needed). over: no-op on everything.

PHASE TIMING: phaseDurationMs = answerMs | hintIntervalMs | revealMs | scoreboardMs | null('over'). phaseKey = 'answer:r{round}' | 'guess:r{round}:h{hintTier}' | 'reveal:r{round}' | 'scoreboard:r{round}' | 'over' — changes per hint tier (re-arms the single alarm, synthesis §1.6 uniqueness rule) and never embeds realIndex or any pick.

VIEW REDACTION MATRIX (viewer may be any string; spectators get the guesser projection minus owned echoes):
- 'answer': answerer sees { role:'mystery', question (real text), answerOptions, myPick: chosenAnswer-echo }. Guessers/spectators see { role:'guesser'|'spectator', mysteryPlayer: PlayerId, scores } — NO question, NO options, NO candidates (an option list could be paired with later candidates to triangulate).
- 'guess': everyone sees { mysteryPlayer, chosenAnswerText (public), candidates: string[], hintTier, hintsRevealed: hints[0..hintTier-1], locked: Record<PlayerId,boolean> (booleans ONLY), scores }. Owner echo myGuess = guesses[viewer] ?? null. The answerer's view additionally carries realIndex (it is their own secret; they hold it in the room anyway). NEVER in any guesser/spectator view: realIndex, any other player's guess value.
- 'reveal': all public — realIndex, per-player { candidateIndex, tier }, gained deltas, voidRound, scores. 'scoreboard'/'over': standings + scores only.
- Tests: leakedSecrets audit treating each player's guess (namespaced candidate token) as an owner secret during 'guess', plus field-level asserts that serialized guesser/spectator views in 'answer' contain no question/options and in 'guess' contain no realIndex/guesses map. Replay test pins the same pack version (synthesis §3.2).

PARAMS SCHEMA for game_config (templateParamsSchema entry, .strict()): { totalRounds: int 1..10?, answerMs: int 10000..45000?, hintTiers: int 2..4?, hintIntervalMs: int 10000..40000?, decoyCount: int 3..6?, tierPoints: int[] length===hintTiers?, readerPointsPerCorrectGuess: int 0..500?, scoreboardEvery: int 1..8? } — future configs (spicy pack variant, 'sprint' 2-tier mode) are Cadence-B content ops on this one module.

BUILD ORDER FIT: slots after the designed four + INPUT_GUESS; reuses Presence/allActed/nextActiveSeat/tally-conventions/gameOver from the kit and the scoreboard:* ad-slot pattern proven by HOT_SEAT. No new event or effect types.

recommendations.question: App-driven progressive hints, player-given hints, or full autonomy without the app? (the co-founder's explicit open question)
recommendations.recommendation: FIRM: app-driven, PRE-AUTHORED progressive hints from the content pack — 2 hints over 3 guess tiers, one revealed per deadline. Reject 'full autonomy' as a product mode, and reject player-given hints as the canonical channel (table talk stays welcome as free social texture: the mystery player's poker face IS an unofficial hint).
recommendations.why: (1) Full autonomy needs no app at all — no timers, no scoring, no reveal beat, no ad slots, no retention; it's a parlor game we'd be giving away, not a Bloop game. (2) Player-given hints violate the never-block rule (a shy or disconnected answerer stalls the room with no deadline semantics), are unscorable, and if typed they open the platform's free-text moderation surface for marginal value. (3) Pre-authored hints are the only version compatible with the deterministic-runtime constraint (no live AI) AND they create the game's signature mechanic: the 300/200/100 tier ladder turns each hint into a risk/reward beat — lock early for glory or wait and play safe. The brief's 'AI gives hints' becomes an offline pipeline that writes the hints into the pack.

recommendations.question: Hint cadence: the brief suggests every 30 seconds — keep it?
recommendations.recommendation: No — 20 seconds per tier (hintIntervalMs=20000), 3 tiers, worst case 60s of guessing, and the phase ends early the moment every connected guesser has locked.
recommendations.why: 30s x 3 tiers = 90s of guessing per round breaks the 'rounds short and TikTok-native' rule (a full round would push 2 minutes). 20s is enough to read 5 candidates and commit, and early-exit-on-allActed means fast tables see ~35-45s rounds in practice.

recommendations.question: How do guessers express 'the question': free text or multiple choice?
recommendations.recommendation: Multiple choice — 1 real question + 4 pre-authored decoys, seed-shuffled per round. Free-text guessing stays out of v1.
recommendations.why: Free text against a target question is undecidable deterministically (normalizeText can't judge 'is this the same question?'), kills scoring fairness, and opens the gameplay-text moderation path. MCQ is fully deterministic, instantly scorable per tier, and the decoys are themselves the comedy ('Who would you call to hide a body?'). Players still shout wild guesses out loud — the room keeps the improv, the app keeps the score.

recommendations.question: Guess locking: last-write-wins (HOT_SEAT's choice) or lock-on-submit?
recommendations.recommendation: Lock-on-submit (first write wins), deliberately diverging from HOT_SEAT §4.1.
recommendations.why: The tier ladder is the game: your points are set by WHEN you lock. If picks were editable, the dominant strategy is to 'park' a guess at tier 0 and edit it after every hint, collapsing the risk/reward into everyone scoring tier-0 points with tier-2 information. Locking makes commitment the skill.

recommendations.question: Does the mystery player score, and does scoring corrupt honest answering?
recommendations.recommendation: Yes: +75 per correct guesser (readerPointsPerCorrectGuess), 0 on a voided round. No honesty enforcement.
recommendations.why: Same alignment trick as HOT_SEAT's readPoints: rewarding the answerer when friends decode them incentivizes picking the answer that is genuinely, recognizably THEM (an arbitrary troll answer scores the answerer nothing). Honesty can't be verified by a reducer anyway — incentive design is the right tool, and 'your friends couldn't find the question' is its own social punishment.

recommendations.question: Is this a config of an existing template (HOT_SEAT) or new code?
recommendations.recommendation: New template REVERSE_GUESS (Cadence A, one deploy), per the honesty standard of the template-architecture doc §3.2. After it ships, variants (spicy pack, 2-tier 'sprint' mode, themed packs) are pure Cadence-B game_configs.
recommendations.why: HOT_SEAT is simultaneous input on a PUBLIC question; this needs sequential answer->guess phases, a per-round redacted secret (realIndex), hint-tier sub-phases with their own deadlines/phaseKeys, and tier-decaying points — a different state machine, far beyond a 'small reducer branch'. Claiming it as config would repeat the '95% zero-code' overstatement that doc explicitly corrects. It reuses the full engine kit and the proven scoreboard ad-slot pattern, so build cost is one game module, zero contract amendments.

recommendations.question: What does the offline AI pipeline actually produce?
recommendations.recommendation: Per item: generate decoy questions and hints, then SCORE cross-plausibility (every answer option must read as a sane answer to the real question AND all 4 decoys; hints must narrow without giving away) — auto-reject items below threshold, then run the standard gate (schema, profanity scan, FR/EN naturalness, replay smoke) before any KV flag flip at rolloutPct 5.
recommendations.why: Decoy quality IS the game's difficulty curve and comedy; humans authoring 40+ cross-plausible items in two locales is the bottleneck. This is exactly the template-architecture §6 pipeline — AI as content op behind the same validation gate as a human, never a runtime dependency.

risks: Decoy quality is load-bearing: weak decoys make tier-0 trivial (everyone scores 300, no tension), over-clever decoys make it a 20% lottery. Mitigation: offline cross-plausibility scoring + the rolloutPct 5% analytics gate (watch correct-rate by tier; target ~25-40% correct at tier 0, ~70%+ by tier 2).

New-template cost: this is Cadence-A code (reducer + client screen + registry entries + redaction tests), not a config-only ship; it should slot into the build order after the engine kit and ideally after one rotation game (HOT_SEAT) has proven nextActiveSeat and the scoreboard ad slot.

Redaction surface: realIndex and the guesses buffer are per-round secrets; a leak (e.g. candidates accidentally ordered real-first, or realIndex in a guesser view) kills the round invisibly. Mandatory leakedSecrets audit + field-level view-serialization tests + seeded candidate shuffle.

Answerer no-show voids the round (deadline or disconnect during 'answer'): correct for never-block, but a flaky host phone could void several rounds; the shell's grace/rejoin handling plus the 20s answer window keep this rare — monitor voided-round rate at 5% rollout.

Worst-case round length is ~88s (20+60+8) if nobody locks early; big rooms (12-16) with slow tables may drag — config lever already exists (hintTiers:2 / hintIntervalMs:15000 'sprint' variant as a Cadence-B config).

Mystery-player trolling (picking a random answer to confuse) is only soft-mitigated by reader points; if analytics show high troll rates, consider a v2 'group calls bluff' verdict — out of scope for v1.
Tier-camping meta: if playtests show everyone waits for hint 2, the 300/200/100 gradient is too flat — tierPoints is a config param, tune without deploy.

Bilingual packs: hints and decoys must be NATURAL in both FR and EN (not translated mush) and the cross-plausibility must hold in BOTH locales independently — the §6 gate must run per locale, doubling curation load.

Item ambiguity vs honesty: answer options must be vague enough to fit 5 questions yet specific enough that the answerer's pick feels personal; this narrow authoring corridor is why the pack needs 40+ vetted items before launch (sizing lint: >= totalRounds, recommended 40+).

phases.description: Turn entry (rides TRUTH_DARE 'choose' with choiceMode:'fixed-action'). The performer (next connected seat in the seeded rotation) stands up. Helpers' phones show the SECRET action text + the constraint card (channel label + rule + forbidden words if taboo). The performer's phone shows ONLY the constraint card and 'Debout ! / Stand up!'. Ends when the performer taps 'Prêt / Ready' or on deadline (auto-advance — a passive performer never blocks). phaseKey = ready:<turnSeq>.

The physical beat (rides TRUTH_DARE 'prompt', promptHiddenFromActive:true). Helpers guide the performer using ONLY the allowed channel (mime / sounds / 3-words / forbidden-words / freeze-frames); the performer physically attempts the action. Performer actions: 'Je l'ai fait ! / I did it!' (declare done) → verdict; 'J'abandonne / Give up' (declare chickened) → score with 0 pts; 'Passer / Pass' (if passesLeft > 0) → score with +2, burns 1 pass. Deadline → auto-fail (0 pts, no pass spent). playerLeft(performer) → auto-fail, advance turn. The action text is NEVER present in the performer's view (leakedSecrets-audited).

Group adjudication (TRUTH_DARE verdict, unchanged). Every connected helper votes 'Réussi / Nailed it' or 'Raté / Failed' — did the performer actually do the action, guided only through the allowed channel? Resolves on all-voted OR deadline (abstainers ignored). doneFraction >= 0.5 → réussi; ties → réussi; zero votes cast → réussi (benefit of the doubt — funny never cruel). Individual votes hidden until score; live view shows counts only (votesIn/votersExpected).

Atomic reveal (TRUTH_DARE score). The action text is finally shown to the performer ('L'action était… / The action was…'), verdict stamp, public tally, points burst: réussi → performer +10, EVERY connected helper +5 (cooperative — new helperPoints param); pass → performer +2; fail/give-up/timeout → 0 for all. Deadline → enterTurn (next performer) or 'over' after totalRounds laps of the rotation (gameOver effect with cloned scores). Lap wrap emits analytics round_completed = the interstitial ad slot; the shell keys the ad off the phaseKey transition.

contentItemShape: One pack item = one (secret action × pre-paired help-channel) card. Authoring shape is bilingual; the publish pipeline splits it into per-locale packs (gda-classic-fr / gda-classic-en) per the platform's single-locale data.locale convention. Shape: { id: string (stable unique, e.g. "gda-party-007"); action: { fr, en } (imperative secret action the performer must end up doing — shown to helpers only until the score reveal); channel: 'mime' | 'sounds' | 'three-words' | 'taboo' | 'statues' (the allowed help channel, curated per item offline); channelLabel: { fr, en } (big public card title, e.g. "MIME UNIQUEMENT" / "MIME ONLY"); channelRule: { fr, en } (one-line rule rendered on every phone); forbiddenWords?: { fr: string[3], en: string[3] } (REQUIRED iff channel === 'taboo'; shown ONLY on helper phones — hidden from the performer like the action); intensity: 'soft' | 'party' | 'spicy' (spicy ships only in a separate 18+ age-gated sibling config); difficulty: 1 | 2 | 3 (pre-computed offline by the AI pipeline, human-reviewed); props: boolean (needs physical objects — filterable); tags: string[] }. Redaction contract: action and forbiddenWords are secrets w.r.t. the performer during ready/act/verdict; everything else is public.

recommendations.question: THE brief's open question: quel mécanisme de 'moyens d'aide autorisés' (cris, mimes… ?) marchera le mieux ?
recommendations.recommendation: A per-round CONSTRAINT CARD ('Canal d'aide') drawn by the app — but pre-paired with each action at authoring time, not rolled independently at runtime. Launch catalog of 5 channels: (1) MIME ONLY — gestures, zero sound (the genre classic); (2) SOUND EFFECTS ONLY — noises/onomatopoeia, no words; (3) 3 WORDS MAX — each helper has a lifetime budget of 3 spoken words this round, phone shows the budget big; (4) FORBIDDEN WORDS (taboo) — helpers talk freely but may never say the 3 forbidden words displayed ONLY on helper phones; (5) FREEZE FRAMES — helpers strike frozen poses and may only re-pose when the performer claps. V2 channels: DRAW IN THE AIR, and ONE MOUTH (the app secretly designates a single helper allowed to speak — a phone-kept sub-role).
recommendations.why: Pre-pairing (offline, AI-assisted, human-reviewed) guarantees every action × channel combo is feasible AND funny — an independent runtime draw produces duds like a sound-based action under a silent channel. It keeps the runtime 100% deterministic (the card is pack data, shuffled by the seeded deck draw TRUTH_DARE already has), gives content ops a difficulty dial, and each card is a recognizable TikTok format. Taboo and One-Mouth are the most phone-native: the phone genuinely acts as secret-keeper, which plain living-room charades can't replicate.

recommendations.question: How is success adjudicated with zero runtime AI and no microphone?
recommendations.recommendation: Reuse the TRUTH_DARE group-verdict machinery verbatim: the performer taps 'I did it!', all connected helpers vote Réussi/Raté within 15s, simple majority with ties and zero-votes resolving to réussi. Deadline always resolves; abstainers are ignored.
recommendations.why: Deterministic, never blocks the room (hard constraint), and peer judgment is itself a party beat. Benefit-of-the-doubt defaults match 'funny never cruel'. Any 'the AI decides if you did it' reading of the brief is redesigned away: the room is the referee, the phone is timer + scorer.

recommendations.question: New template or reuse? (catalog-economics call)
recommendations.recommendation: Ship as TRUTH_DARE@2 — a new-params evolution, NOT a new template and NOT zero-code. New params: promptHiddenFromActive (redacts action text + forbiddenWords from the performer's view), choiceMode:'fixed-action' (skips the Truth/Dare choose phase; repurposes it as the 6s ready beat), helperPoints (cooperative scoring). Content entries gain channel/channelLabel/channelRule/forbiddenWords fields.
recommendations.why: Rotation, turnSeq phaseKey, declare→verdict→score, pass economy, intensity tiers, deck-draw-without-repeat, presence handling and all timeout behaviors map 1:1 onto TRUTH_DARE as designed. The single structural delta is one view-redaction branch + a leakedSecrets test. This follows the architecture doc's own precedent (NPC Infiltrator = content shape + one small param on SECRET_ROLE), and after this deploy every future variant (themed packs, spicy pack) is pure Cadence-B config/content.

recommendations.question: Helpers score +5 on réussi — doesn't that bias the verdict to 'yes'?
recommendations.recommendation: Accept the generosity bias in v1 and keep helper points contingent on réussi; make the tally public at score so trolling/rubber-stamping is socially visible. Monitor the réussi-rate analytic; if it exceeds ~95% the verdict is dead theater — then add a third verdict option 'on a triché / we cheated' (voids helper points, performer keeps theirs) as a TRUTH_DARE@2.1 param.
recommendations.why: It's a cooperative game: the verdict's real job is stopping blatant fails and channel cheating, not precision refereeing. A punitive accurate-verdict economy would incentivize voting friends down — exactly the cruelty the brand book forbids.

recommendations.question: Session length and round structure?
recommendations.recommendation: One 'round' as players perceive it = one performer turn, ~75s typical (6 ready + ~45 act, usually ended early by 'I did it!' + 15 verdict + 7 score; 103s absolute worst case). params.totalRounds = 2 laps of the rotation (everyone performs twice) for rooms of 3–7 → 8–14 min sessions; recommend a hostTunable or auto-scale to 1 lap at 8+ players. Pass economy: 1 pass per player (escape hatch for an action you really won't do).
recommendations.why: Keeps the session TikTok-native (many ~75s beats), and the deadline chain guarantees a disconnected or frozen performer costs the room at most one act-timer before the rotation moves on.

recommendations.question: Spicy content?
recommendations.recommendation: Default config ships soft+party only (spicyLevel 0). A separate sibling game_config ('devine-l-action-spicy') pins an 18+ pack with tone:'spicy', minAge:18, behind the platform age gate — same template, pure config.
recommendations.why: Physical dares escalate fast; keeping spice in a separate age-gated catalog entry matches the gameConfigSchema refinement (spicy ⇒ minAge ≥ 18) and store compliance, with zero extra code.

risks: Redaction is the load-bearing surface: the secret action text and taboo forbiddenWords must NEVER appear in the performer's view during ready/act/verdict (only at score reveal). Mandatory leakedSecrets audit treating both as secrets w.r.t. the active player, plus a field-level test that the serialized performer view contains no action/forbiddenWords strings.

Not pure Cadence-B: requires a TRUTH_DARE@2 code deploy (promptHiddenFromActive, choiceMode, helperPoints params + content-schema fields) before the config can ship. Small, but it is new reducer/view code on the template, not zero code.

Verdict generosity bias: helpers profit from voting réussi, so the verdict skews yes. Accepted by design (cooperative), but track réussi-rate analytics; >95% means the verdict phase is pure theater and needs the 'we cheated' third option.

Channel enforcement is social-only — the app cannot hear the room. The constraint card must be unmissable on every phone (big label + 1-line rule every phase) and the verdict copy must say 'vote Raté if the helpers cheated the channel'.

Physical safety: actions are performed for real in a living room. The offline pipeline must lint out risky verbs (climbing, chugging, running blindfolded, anything involving non-players) and a human must review every pack; props:true items must be filterable per room.

Pack sizing: deck-draw-without-repeat needs >= maxPlayers x totalRounds entries per intensity tier (16 x 2 = 32 minimum; author 60+ per tier per locale) or the game ends early on pool exhaustion (graceful, but short).

3-player floor: with only 2 helpers, mime/sounds/taboo still work but the verdict is a 2-vote majority and the ONE MOUTH channel degenerates — that channel is correctly deferred to v2 and should carry a minPlayers hint in pack data.

Disconnects: performer leaving mid-act resolves as fail-and-advance (never blocks); but a wave of helper disconnects during verdict can empty the voter set → resolves réussi by default, which a griefing duo could exploit in tiny rooms. Acceptable at this stakes level; monitor.

taglineFr: Complète la phrase, vise le pourcentage de la foule.
taglineEn: Finish the line, hit the crowd's number.

phases.description: All phones show the round's sentence stem, the ANNOUNCED target split in huge type (e.g. 'Vise 80% OUI / Aim for 80% YES'), and the item's 6 completion cards (display order shuffled once per round from the seeded RNG at init — deterministic and identical for all viewers). Each player secretly taps ONE card; picks live in a HIDDEN buffer (picks: Record<PlayerId, cardIndex>), never visible to other viewers; owner echo is picks[viewer] ?? null. Early-resolve via allActed(connectedPlayers(roster, connected), picks). TIMEOUT: at the deadline the round resolves with whoever picked; non-pickers and disconnected players simply score 0 this round (never auto-assigned a card, never block the room). phaseKey = pick:r{round}.

Atomic reveal: cards flip to show their pre-computed crowdYesPct, player avatars land on their picked cards, and each card shows its distance d = |crowdYesPct - targetYesPct|. SCORING (exact): every player whose card has the MINIMUM d among picked-able cards (all 6 cards count for distance ranking, but only players who picked score) gets +closestPoints (3); every player on the card with the SECOND-smallest distinct d gets +secondPoints (1); if the winning card's d <= bullseyeWindowPct (2), its pickers each get +bullseyeBonus (2) on top (so a bullseye round pays 5). Distance ties: all tied cards count as 'closest' and all their pickers get the full +3 (no splitting). Non-pickers: 0. Running scores shown. TIMEOUT: deadline auto-advances to the next round's pick, or to 'over' after totalRounds; emits analytics round_completed at the boundary (shell ad cue is the phaseKey transition itself, per synthesis §5.4). phaseKey = reveal:r{round}.

Terminal scoreboard. Untimed (phaseDurationMs returns null), phaseKey = 'over'. Emits the gameOver effect with a defensively CLONED final scores map (gameOver(scores) kit helper). Highest total wins the match; the shell converts placement (not raw points) into session XP per the cross-game convention. Shell may fire the interstitial off the -> over phaseKey transition.

contentItemShape:
One pack item = one round. Authoring (bilingual) shape — the offline pipeline splits it into the platform's single-locale runtime packs (data.locale per synthesis §3.1: cinquante-cinquante-fr / cinquante-cinquante-en) and re-estimates percentages PER LOCALE:

{
  "id": string (kebab, stable, e.g. "cc-honestly-001"),
  "targetYesPct": int 1..99 — the ANNOUNCED target split for the round ("aim for 80% YES"); authored per item so packs cover extremes (95/5) and coin-flips (50/50),
  "askKind": "didYou" | "agree" | "wouldYou" — how the (fictional, consistent) crowd of 1,000 polled people was asked about each completed sentence: 'is this true for you?' / 'do you agree?' / 'would/could you?'. Drives the reveal copy ("84% de la foule a dit OUI"),
  "stem": { "fr": string, "en": string } — sentence opener shown big, ends with an ellipsis,
  "completions": exactly cardsPerRound (6) entries, each {
    "id": string ("a".."f"),
    "text": { "fr": string, "en": string } — completes the stem grammatically in BOTH languages,
    "crowdYesPct": int 0..100 — PRE-COMPUTED offline (LLM persona-ensemble estimate calibrated on real published polls; provenance stored; never computed at runtime),
    "spicy": 0|1|2 optional (default 0; >0 only allowed in spicy packs)
  },
  "tone": "classic" | "spicy" (default classic),
  "tags": string[] optional (curation only; reducer ignores)
}

Pipeline lints (AI gate, hard): all 6 crowdYesPct pairwise distinct by >=3 EXCEPT at most one designed tie pair vs the target; at least one card within 12 of targetYesPct (a winnable round); at most one card inside the bullseye window; pack size >= totalRounds * 9 (~63 items) so no-repeat draw never exhausts a session streak; every string passes the obscenity filter; FR and EN both natural (human gate before rolloutPct > 5).

recommendations.question: The brief wants the AI to score each player's free-text completion LIVE. How do we keep the mechanic without runtime AI?
recommendations.recommendation: Replace free-text + live judging with a pack-authored hand: each item ships a stem, an announced target split, and 6 pre-written completions each carrying a PRE-COMPUTED crowdYesPct. Players pick the completion they believe lands closest to the target; the reveal flips the true numbers. All three beats of the brief survive: complete the stem, crowd %, closest-to-announced-target wins.
recommendations.why: The engine contract (packages/engine/src/types.ts) forbids any I/O, wall-clock, or ambient randomness in game code; all nondeterminism enters via seed + event timestamps. Live LLM scoring is impossible to replay deterministically; pre-scored cards are.

recommendations.question: Where do the crowd percentages come from, and will players trust them?
recommendations.recommendation: Offline pipeline: an LLM persona-ensemble (>=20 sampled demographic personas per locale, majority-vote, temperature-varied) estimates each completion's YES %, calibrated against real published polls (YouGov/Ifop-style anchors) with provenance stored per item. Frame it in-game as a consistent fictional crowd: 'On a sondé 1 000 personnes' / 'We polled 1,000 people'. Human spot-check is gate stage 5 before rolloutPct rises.
recommendations.why: A contested number ('no way 84% ate floor food!') is actually the fun if the crowd is a consistent character — but only if the numbers are plausible. Calibration + the AI-packaging gate (template-architecture §6) keeps them defensible without ever running AI at gameplay time.

recommendations.question: The brief says the target is 'pas nécessairement 50/50 : 80/20, 95/5'. How are targets chosen?
recommendations.recommendation: targetYesPct is authored per item with a pack-level distribution lint: ~1/3 extreme targets (>=90 or <=10), ~1/3 mid (60-85 / 15-40), ~1/3 near coin-flip (40-60). Round order is the seeded shuffle, so every session mixes target flavors. Lint: at least one card within 12 of target, at most one card inside the bullseye window.
recommendations.why: Extreme targets (95/5) play completely differently from coin-flips and are the brief's signature; authoring + lint guarantees the variety instead of hoping the AI generator produces it.

recommendations.question: New template or reuse?
recommendations.recommendation: Ship as a third mode of INPUT_GUESS: params.mode = 'crowd-target', growing the mode enum in templateParamsSchema plus optional params (pickMs, revealMs, cardsPerRound, point values). Crucially, this mode has ZERO free text, so it can be the FIRST INPUT_GUESS mode built — it needs none of the gameplay-text moderation surface that gates blitz/collab-one-word (template-architecture §3.3).
recommendations.why: The architecture doc's ruling is modes-within-one-template (cf. impostorWordMode, ToD intensities). crowd-target shares the INPUT_GUESS skeleton exactly: per-round prompt, hidden simultaneous buffer, atomic reveal, scoring against pack data — and it de-risks the missing template by shipping its easiest mode first.

recommendations.question: Can we ever get the original free-completion creativity back?
recommendations.recommendation: Yes, as a v2 'freestyle' sibling mode: players TYPE their own completion, then the ROOM itself votes OUI/NON on each completion live, and the room's % is the score against the target — closest wins. Deterministic (the crowd is the room), no AI, but it requires the hardened text-moderation path, so schedule it after collab-one-word ships.
recommendations.why: It recovers the brief's creative beat with the room as the crowd — fully deterministic — and slots into the same template as one more mode, no contract change.

recommendations.question: Ties, passive players, disconnects?
recommendations.recommendation: Distance ties: all tied-closest cards pay full closestPoints to their pickers (no splitting — sample item 3 demonstrates a designed 27-vs-33 tie at target 30). Deadline non-pickers score 0 and are never auto-assigned a card. Disconnected players are excluded from allActed's expected set (connectedPlayers), so the phase early-resolves without them; playerLeft never deletes the roster seat or touches scores.
recommendations.why: Platform rule: a disconnected or passive player must never block the room (spec §6 / synthesis §1.3); full-points ties keep the reveal celebratory, never punitive — 'funny never cruel'.

recommendations.question: Same percentages for FR and EN?
recommendations.recommendation: No — the pipeline re-estimates crowdYesPct per locale when splitting the bilingual authoring source into the single-locale runtime packs (cinquante-cinquante-fr / -en, per the data.locale convention). Rooms are single-locale, so fairness within a room is unaffected.
recommendations.why: FR and EN crowds genuinely answer differently (pineapple pizza polls differently in Paris and Portland); per-locale numbers keep the fictional crowd credible, and the platform already mandates one locale per pack id (synthesis §3.1/§3.3).

recommendations.question: Spicy version?
recommendations.recommendation: Default pack is tone classic / minAge 0 (this design, spicyLevel 0). Ship a sibling config 'cinquante-cinquante-after-dark' later: tone spicy, minAge 18, spicy completions only in that pack — same template, same params, pure Cadence-B content op.
recommendations.why: Age-gating is a catalog/config concern (gameConfigSchema refinement: spicy => minAge >= 18); keeping the launch pack safe maximizes reach while the spicy sibling is a zero-code follow-up.

risks: Gated on template build: INPUT_GUESS is the one missing template (no module exists yet — template-architecture §3.1). Mitigation: crowd-target is its simplest mode (no text input, no moderation), so it can be the first INPUT_GUESS slice built; everything else (hidden buffer, allActed, phaseKey, tally-style reveal) is proven kit.

Crowd percentages are AI estimates and will be contested by players ('84%? no way!'). Mitigation: calibrate against real polls, store provenance, frame the crowd as a consistent fictional 1,000-person panel, and lean into the argument as the party moment — but a sloppy pack kills trust fast, so the human gate (stage 5) is load-bearing.

Content burn: once a group has seen an item's percentages, the round is dead for them. Packs need >= ~63 items (totalRounds x 9 sessions lint), no-repeat seeded draw within a session, and a steady offline-pipeline cadence of fresh packs (Cadence B, no deploy).

Bilingual authoring vs single-locale runtime: the platform mandates one locale per pack id; the pipeline MUST split the bilingual source and re-estimate percentages per locale, or FR rooms get EN-calibrated numbers.

Readability at speed: 6 cards + a target + a stem in 25s on a phone is the ceiling; with cardsPerRound > 6 or verbose completions the pick phase degrades. Lint completion length (<= ~60 chars/locale) and keep cardsPerRound at 4-6.
Tie-sharing point inflation: full points to all tied pickers is generous; the pairwise >=3-distinct lint bounds it to at most one designed tie per item.

phaseKey/secret hygiene: picks are secrets until reveal — they must never appear in phaseKey or any non-owner view; redaction tests via leakedSecrets on the picks buffer are mandatory (synthesis §1.5 convention).

taglineFr: Une question vérité : tu réponds... ou tu bois. Santé !
taglineEn: One truth question: answer it... or drink. Cheers!

phases.description: AUTO-SKIPPED in this config. TRUTH_DARE@2 param allowedChoices=['truth'] resolves the choice instantly on turn entry (no UI beat, no timer, no auto-pick coin needed) and draws the truth question from the seeded no-repeat truth deck. phaseKey goes straight to prompt:<turnSeq>. The classic truth-or-dare configs keep allowedChoices=['truth','dare'] and are untouched.

The truth question appears on every phone (everyone reads it; the fun is in the room). The active player answers OUT LOUD, then taps 'I answered' (-> verdict) — or taps the escape button 'Je bois / I drink' (escapeMode='forfeit-draw': unlimited, ignores the pass economy, draws one forfeit card from the dare deck and jumps straight to score with +3 pts). TIMEOUT (deadline): scored as dodged — 0 points, NO forfeit drawn or assigned (never auto-assign alcohol to a passive or disconnected player); the room never blocks. If the active player disconnects mid-prompt, same: dodged, 0 pts, next turn (template playerLeft rule).

Reached ONLY after an 'I answered' claim. Every present non-active player votes 'Vraie réponse / Real answer' vs 'Esquive / Dodged' (allActed over connected-minus-active). Resolves early when all eligible voters voted. TIMEOUT: tally whatever votes are in; abstainers excluded; ZERO votes cast -> 'answered' (benefit of the doubt — funny never cruel). Ties resolve to 'answered' (>= verdictThreshold 0.5). Individual votes stay HIDDEN (counts only, votesIn/votersExpected) until score — tracer redaction rule. Eligible set empty (e.g. 2-player room, other player disconnected) -> instant 'answered'.

Reveal card. EXACT SCORING: verdicted real answer -> +10 (donePoints) to the active player; drink/forfeit taken -> +3 (passPoints) to the active player + the forfeit card is displayed ('Une gorgée ! / One sip!' in the drink pack, a 10-second gage in the safe sibling); dodged (verdicted down) or timeout -> 0 (chickenedPoints). dareBonus=0 (no dare choice exists). Voters NEVER score (keeps the verdict honest, per ToD design §5). Deadline auto-advances to the next present player's turn (nextActiveSeat, skips disconnected seats); a rotation-lap wrap emits analytics 'round_completed' (the shell's interstitial-ad boundary, keyed off the phaseKey transition); after lap totalRounds=2 -> 'over' + gameOver(cloned scores).

contentItemShape: One authoring item in the bilingual master pack (the offline splitter emits two single-locale runtime packs, truth-or-drink-fr and truth-or-drink-en, with data.locale per cross-game-synthesis §3.1; runtime text is the plain single-locale string): { id: string — stable unique id, the no-repeat key, e.g. 'totd-t-party-014'; choice: 'truth' | 'dare' — 'truth' rows are the questions, 'dare' rows are the FORFEIT POOL drawn when the active player escapes (sip instructions in the 18+ drink pack; 10-second gages in the safe truth-or-forfeit sibling pack) — this reuses the TRUTH_DARE deck machinery with zero new content schema; intensity: 'soft' | 'party' | 'spicy' — the drink config draws party+spicy, the safe sibling soft+party; text: { fr: string, en: string } — shown verbatim, pre-moderated (passes the obscenity scan + alcohol-excess lint at authoring time); minAge?: number — 18 on EVERY row of the drink pack; tags?: string[] — freeform curation hints like 'drink','forfeit','dating','phone','funny'. Sizing lint: >= maxPlayers x totalRounds (16x2=32) truth rows per allowed intensity tier and >= 16 forfeit rows per tier (synthesis §3.5).

recommendations.question: The brief's open ask: design the drink vs forfeit (gage) toggle for the non-drinking variant.
recommendations.recommendation: Ship TWO sibling game_configs on the same TRUTH_DARE@2 module sharing the truth-question pack family: 'truth-or-drink' (tone='spicy', minAge=18, forfeit pool = one-sip drink cards, party+spicy tiers) and 'truth-or-forfeit' (tone='classic', minAge=0, forfeit pool = 10-second gage cards, soft+party tiers). The 'toggle' is which Home tile the group taps — NOT a lobby host switch.
recommendations.why: Age-gating is per-config in the catalog and schema-enforced (spicy => minAge>=18, template-architecture §2.1 refinement c); one tile cannot be both 18+ and store-safe. A sibling config costs one KV entry + one forfeit pool — zero code (Cadence B). It also makes the safe variant the discoverable default for under-18 devices instead of a buried setting.

recommendations.question: How does this reconcile with the existing truth-or-dare design (same template?).
recommendations.recommendation: Same TRUTH_DARE module, bumped to @2 with three ADDITIVE params: allowedChoices (['truth'] auto-resolves the choose phase — 0ms, straight to prompt:<turnSeq>), escapeMode ('pass' default = ToD's limited skip economy unchanged | 'forfeit-draw' = escape unlimited, passesLeft ignored, draws one card from the dare deck shown at score), and labels (localized client copy overrides for the escape/claim/verdict buttons). Existing truth-or-dare configs keep all defaults and are untouched; templateParamsSchema for TRUTH_DARE grows accordingly in packages/protocol.
recommendations.why: This is exactly the template-architecture's sanctioned 'new-params' pattern (like VOTE revealStyle for Pass the Bloop, §3.2 #7): a small reducer/view branch on a module being built anyway (synthesis build slot #3), versus a duplicate module re-implementing rotation, verdict, presence and deck draws. The forfeit pool reusing choice:'dare' rows means zero new content schema and zero new redaction surface.

recommendations.question: Should the room also verdict-vote whether the player actually drank?
recommendations.recommendation: No. Drinking/doing the forfeit resolves instantly via the template's pass path (skip verdict, +3, show the forfeit card). The verdict only adjudicates a contested 'I answered' claim (Real answer vs Dodged).
recommendations.why: The drink is physically visible to the whole room — a vote on it is dead air. This mirrors the ToD design's own rationale ('a self-admitted chicken skips the vote', §4 prompt table) and keeps the turn at ~40s typical.

recommendations.question: Timeout and disconnect semantics on the question.
recommendations.recommendation: Prompt deadline or active-player disconnect = 'dodged': 0 points, NO forfeit drawn, advance to next present player. Verdict deadline = tally votes in (zero votes -> answered).
recommendations.why: Hard platform rule: a passive or disconnected player must never block the room, and the game must never assign alcohol to someone who isn't actually there. 0 points also removes any incentive to idle through your turn.

recommendations.question: Responsible-drinking guardrails (18+ alcohol pack).
recommendations.recommendation: Every drink forfeit is capped at 'one sip' phrasing; the offline authoring lint rejects chug / 'cul sec' / quantity-escalation wording; the lobby for this config shows a persistent footer ('Bois de l'eau, ne conduis pas — les softs comptent' / 'Drink water, don't drive — soft drinks count'); answering is ALWAYS available so drinking is never forced; the truth-or-forfeit sibling is the promoted non-alcohol path.
recommendations.why: Brand rule 'funny never cruel' + Apple 1.4.3 / Google alcohol-content compliance. The lint slots into the existing offline content gate (template-architecture §6 step 3) as one extra rule — no runtime cost.

recommendations.question: Session length: 2 laps at 16 players is 32 turns (~25 min).
recommendations.recommendation: Keep totalRounds=2 laps as the default (typical 4-8 player room = 8-16 turns, ~8-12 min), and tighten to 1 lap when the lobby roster is >= 10 (a config-level scaling rule, same open question as ToD §9 Q8). Lean on the 'play again' CTA for many-quick-rounds sessions.
recommendations.why: Rounds must stay TikTok-native; one spotlight turn is the atomic ~45s beat, and a session should be several short games, not one marathon. Lap wrap is also the interstitial boundary, so 2 laps = exactly 1 mid-session ad.

risks: Store compliance (alcohol): the config MUST ship tone='spicy' + minAge=18 (schema-enforced) behind the device age gate, with possible region flags; under-18 devices only ever see the truth-or-forfeit sibling. Apple 1.4.3 / Google content-rating review is a launch dependency.

Not pure config: requires TRUTH_DARE@2 additive params (allowedChoices, escapeMode, labels) — a small reducer/view branch plus templateParamsSchema growth in packages/protocol. Schedule with the truth-or-dare module build (synthesis build order slot #3); until then this tile cannot ship.

Excessive-drinking liability: mitigated by one-sip-only forfeit copy, the authoring lint against chug/escalation wording, the water/no-driving lobby footer, and the fact that answering is always available — but a final product+legal sign-off is required before the spicy pack goes live (same gate as ToD §9 Q2).

Verdict griefing: the room can vote a genuine answer as 'Dodged' (0 pts). Mitigations inherited from the template: ties resolve to 'answered', votes are unscored, individual votes are never revealed (counts only). Monitor 'verdict_resolved' analytics for dogpiling patterns.

Pack exhaustion: 16 players x 2 laps = 32 truth draws per game — packs need >= 32 truth rows per allowed intensity tier and >= 16 forfeit rows per tier (synthesis §3.5 lint); tier exhaustion falls back down (spicy->party) then ends the game gracefully ('pool_exhausted').

Spoken answers happen off-platform and are unmoderated: questions must never target identifiable third parties or solicit medical/illegal/doxxing confessions — enforced as an authoring rule in the offline safety scan ('funny never cruel').

2-player rooms make the verdict a single judge (inherited ToD §9 Q6). Acceptable for the classic pair format (the original 'Truth or Drink' is literally played in pairs), but consider advisory-only verdicts below 3 players if playtests feel punitive.

taglineFr: L'un mime le délire, l'autre le double en direct — le salon note le duo.
taglineEn: One friend does the move, the other dubs it live — the room rates the duo.

phases.description: Secret pick. The mover (X) sees 2 movement prompts on their phone and picks one (the brief's 'Joueur X choisit'). The dubber (Y) sees a 'YOU ARE THE VOICE' role card — never the prompt. The audience sees 'X is choosing a secret move'. Timeout: auto-pick option A (deterministic, offer[0]). Mover disconnects: turn voided, rotation advances. Dubber disconnects: reassigned to next connected seat.

The standup beat — phones down. X performs the movement in the middle of the room; Y improvises the live sound dub, BLIND (Y never saw the prompt — that mismatch is the comedy engine). All phones show a big countdown; both crew members can tap 'Done' to end early (allActed over connected crew). Timeout: proceed to rating. Mover leaves: turn voided. Dubber leaves: performance finishes solo, scoring proceeds.

Audience stars. Every connected non-crew player casts 1–5 stars into a hidden buffer (first tap locks; counts shown as 'votesIn/votersExpected', never values). Crew sees a suspense card and cannot rate. Ends all-acted or deadline; ballots cast at deadline are used, 0 ballots → default 3.0 stars. Empty audience at phase entry resolves immediately with the default. A leaving rater shrinks the expected set (never stalls the room).

The second laugh beat. The secret prompt text flips public for everyone ('THAT was supposed to be a cat?!'), star average + cast count shown, +points burst for BOTH duo members (identical score), ovation badge if unanimous 5 stars. Lap wrap emits analytics round_completed — the shell's interstitial ad boundary. Timeout: next turn (next connected mover, dubber = following seat) or 'over' with gameOver(cloned scores).

contentItemShape: One movement prompt (the secret shown to the mover). Shape: { id: string — stable unique id, e.g. "dlm-001-robot-hiphop" (no-repeat + report/kill-switch key); text: { fr: string, en: string } — the movement/choreography/mime to perform, max 120 chars, shown ONLY to the mover until reveal; hint: { fr: string, en: string } — optional one-line performance tip rendered under the prompt, mover-only, max 120 chars; category: "animals" | "dance" | "sports" | "everyday" | "cinema" | "cringe"; difficulty: 1 | 2 | 3 — curation metadata, ignored by the reducer; intensity: "safe" | "spicy" — spicy entries ship in a separate age-gated pack (tone:"spicy", minAge 18) and are excluded by DEFAULT_CONFIG allowedIntensities:["safe"]; props: boolean — needs physical objects (filterable); tags: string[] max 8 — freeform ("funny","physical","meme","tiktok"). Authoring/publish note: items are authored bilingual {fr,en} as shown; the publish pipeline splits them into single-locale packs per platform convention (data.locale, pack family "double-le-mouvement-fr" / "-en", shell resolves locale at startGame). Pool sizing lint (synthesis §3.5): >= laps x maxPlayers x promptChoices = 32 entries minimum per intensity tier at defaults.

newTemplateSpec:
TEMPLATE PERFORM_RATE (module id "perform-rate", version 1) — rotating performance crew + audience star rating. Generic: crewSize 1 (solo mime/charades configs) or 2 (this game: mover X + dubber Y). Pure GameModule<S,A,V,C> per packages/engine/src/types.ts; imports the shared kit (emptyPlayerMap, Presence/connectedPlayers, allActed, nextActiveSeat, gameOver helper) per cross-game synthesis §1. No new event or effect types; no wall-clock, no ambient RNG (all randomness via createRng(seed+'|rot') for rotation, createRng(seed+'|deck') for the prompt deck).

CONFIG (templateParamsSchema addition, .strict()): { crewSize: 1|2 (default 2); laps: int 1..3 (1); promptChoices: int 1..3 (2); briefMs 5000..30000 (15000); performMs 10000..60000 (30000); rateMs 5000..30000 (15000); revealMs 3000..15000 (7000); starMultiplier int 5..50 (20); ovationBonus int 0..100 (25); noVoteDefaultStars 1..5 (3); allowedIntensities ('safe'|'spicy')[] (['safe']) }.

STATE (all player-keyed maps null-proto via emptyPlayerMap; JSON-safe only):
PRState = { config; players: PlayerId[] (fixed roster); rotation: PlayerId[] (seeded permutation = mover order); connected: Presence; phase: 'brief'|'perform'|'rate'|'reveal'|'over'; turnSeq: number (monotonic, ++ per turn entry — powers phaseKey); turnIndex: number; lap: number; totalTurns: number (= min(laps*players.length, floor(deck.length/promptChoices)) at init); turnsPlayed: number; mover: PlayerId; dubber: PlayerId|null; voidTurn: boolean; deck: string[] /* HIDDEN: seeded shuffle of prompt ids — leaks upcoming prompts */; cursor: number /* HIDDEN */; offer: string[] /* HIDDEN until reveal: the promptChoices ids offered this turn */; chosenId: string|null /* HIDDEN until reveal */; doneTaps: Record<PlayerId,true> (public booleans, crew only); stars: Record<PlayerId,1|2|3|4|5> /* HIDDEN: audience ballots; promoted at reveal as AGGREGATE only, individual ballots never published */; scores: Record<PlayerId,number>; lastResult: { mover; dubber; promptText; avg; cast; ovation; points }|null }.

ACTIONS (zod at DO boundary + reducer guards; zero free text → zero gameplay moderation surface):
PRAction = { kind:'pick'; index:number } (brief; mover only; 0<=index<promptChoices) | { kind:'done' } (perform; crew only; idempotent) | { kind:'rate'; stars:1|2|3|4|5 } (rate; connected non-crew only; FIRST WRITE LOCKS, duplicates ignored).

EVENTS: standard GameEvent only (action/deadline/playerLeft/playerRejoined). Effects: analytics ('turn_started','prompt_picked'|'prompt_auto','rating_resolved'{avg,cast,ovation},'crew_left','round_completed' on lap wrap = the shell's ad boundary,'pool_exhausted') and gameOver with cloned scores. Rejected events return the SAME state reference (shell no-op contract).

PHASE MACHINE (one turn = brief→perform→rate→reveal; rejection = same-ref no-op; over short-circuits at top of reduce):
ENTER TURN (from init or reveal deadline): turnIndex = nextActiveSeat(rotation, prev, connected); on wrap lap++ and emit round_completed if continuing; if turnsPlayed>=totalTurns or lap>=laps → phase 'over' + gameOver({...scores}). mover=rotation[turnIndex]; dubber = next connected seat after mover excluding mover (null if none → solo fallback); offer = deck[cursor..cursor+promptChoices), cursor+=promptChoices (exhausted → 'over' + pool_exhausted); turnSeq++; stars/doneTaps reset; chosenId=null; voidTurn=false; phase='brief'.
brief: pick by mover w/ valid index → chosenId=offer[index], phase='perform'. deadline → chosenId=offer[0] (deterministic auto-pick), phase='perform'. playerLeft(mover) → voidTurn → ENTER TURN (crew_left). playerLeft(dubber) → reassign next connected non-mover seat or null.
perform: done by crew → doneTaps[p]=true; allActed(connectedCrew, doneTaps) → phase='rate'. deadline → phase='rate'. playerLeft(mover) → voidTurn → ENTER TURN; playerLeft(dubber) → continue (solo finish, scoring unchanged — the room's stars judge it).
rate (entry guard: expected = connectedPlayers minus crew; empty → resolve immediately with noVoteDefaultStars): rate by expected w/o prior ballot → stars[p]=v; allActed(expected,stars) → RESOLVE. deadline → RESOLVE with cast ballots. playerLeft(rater) → shrink expected, re-check allActed.
RESOLVE: cast=values(stars); avg = cast.length ? mean(cast) : noVoteDefaultStars; points = round(avg*starMultiplier); if cast.length>=2 && all===5 → ovation, points+=ovationBonus. If !voidTurn: scores[mover]+=points AND if dubber!=null scores[dubber]+=points (identical duo score — cooperative by construction). lastResult set (avg to 1 decimal); turnsPlayed++; phase='reveal'; analytics rating_resolved.
reveal: actions ignored; deadline → ENTER TURN.

phaseDurationMs: brief→briefMs, perform→performMs, rate→rateMs, reveal→revealMs, over→null. phaseKey: `${phase}:${turnSeq}`, terminal 'over' (synthesis §1.6 turn-rotation rule; never embeds prompt ids/text — secret-safe per types.ts).

VIEW REDACTION (viewer may be ANY string; spectator-safe). Common scaffolding all phases: phase, turnSeq, lap/laps, turnsPlayed/totalTurns, rotation, connected, mover, dubber, scores.
brief: mover → offers [{id,text,hint}] (the ONLY view ever containing undisclosed prompt text) + myPick echo. dubber → role:'dubber' card, NO prompt data. audience/unknown → role:'audience', NO prompt data.
perform: mover → chosenPrompt {text,hint} (own-secret echo) + Done state. dubber → 'DUB IT LIVE' card + doneTaps booleans, NO prompt. others/unknown → 'watch the show' + countdown + doneTaps booleans.
rate: audience member → star picker + myStars echo (own ballot ?? null, never a foreign lookup) + votesIn/votersExpected COUNTS only. crew/unknown → suspense card + counts, myStars:null. No viewer ever sees another's star value or any prompt data.
reveal: IDENTICAL public view for all: lastResult (promptText now public, avg, cast, ovation, points), scores, nextMover|null. over: identical final scores/standings.
Hidden-forever: deck, cursor. Hidden-until-reveal: offer, chosenId. Hidden-always-as-individuals: stars (aggregate only). leakedSecrets audit: each offered/chosen prompt text = mover-owned secret until reveal; each star ballot = rater-owned secret forever.

BOUNDS: template minPlayers 3 (mover+dubber+1 rater), maxPlayers 16; this game's config tightens to 4..16. TESTS: (phase,event) table; leakedSecrets as above; field-level 'rate-phase serialized view contains no stars map'; edges 3 & 16 players; mover/dubber disconnect per phase; empty-audience entry; deck exhaustion; same-seed determinism; gameOver no-alias; same-ref rejection. CLIENT (mobile gameRegistry): SecretPick (mover) / RoleCard (dubber, audience) for brief; CountdownStage for perform; StarRater for rate; RevealCard for reveal. REUSE (config-only future games): solo mime rating (crewSize 1), air-band duo (music pack), slow-mo replay (everyday pack, longer performMs), spicy dance pack (intensity gate, minAge 18).

recommendations.question: How does the app prompt X with the secret movement (the brief says 'Joueur X choisit')?
recommendations.recommendation: A 15s 'brief' phase shows X two pack prompts on their phone, secretly; X taps one. Deadline auto-picks option A deterministically.
recommendations.why: A curated 2-option pick preserves the brief's player agency ('choisit') without the blank-page stall of free invention, keeps content pack-driven (deterministic, moderated, replayable), and the timeout guarantees a passive X never blocks the room.

recommendations.question: Does Y (the dubber) see the prompt before or during the dub?
recommendations.recommendation: Never — Y dubs blind. Y's phone shows only a 'YOU ARE THE VOICE' role card and the perform countdown; the prompt reaches Y at reveal like everyone else.
recommendations.why: The comedic engine is the mismatch between movement and improvised sound; an informed dubber collapses into narration. It also halves the redaction surface: only the mover's views ever carry undisclosed prompt text.

recommendations.question: How does the room score the duo?
recommendations.recommendation: Each connected non-crew player casts 1-5 stars into a hidden buffer (first tap locks). BOTH duo members earn round(avg x 20) points (20-100); unanimous 5-star with >=2 ballots adds +25 ovation bonus each; zero ballots default to 3.0 stars. Rating itself earns nothing.
recommendations.why: Identical duo scores make it cooperative (X picks performable moves, Y commits to the bit); the 20-point floor and 3-star default blunt trolling and AFK rooms; unscored ratings stay honest (same rationale as truth-or-dare's unscored verdict).

recommendations.question: When is the secret prompt revealed to the room?
recommendations.recommendation: Only AFTER stars lock, during the reveal phase.
recommendations.why: The room rates the comedy of the performance, not fidelity to a prompt it could second-guess — and the reveal becomes a guaranteed second laugh beat ('THAT was supposed to be a cat?!').

recommendations.question: Player count and session length?
recommendations.recommendation: Config minPlayers 4 (template floor 3), sweet spot 4-10; default laps=1 so everyone is mover exactly once and dubber ~once (dubber = next connected seat). At ~67s/turn a 6-player session is ~7 min.
recommendations.why: At 3 players the audience is a single rater (swingy, gameable); at 16 players one lap is ~18 min — acceptable but long, so the catalog copy should steer big rooms elsewhere or a config variant can cap turns.

recommendations.question: Should the audience also guess what the prompt was (extra mechanic)?
recommendations.recommendation: Defer to v2 as an optional param (typed guess before reveal, closest wins bonus points). v1 ships enum-only actions.
recommendations.why: A guess phase adds the platform's free-text moderation surface (DO obscenity filter, normalizeText compare) and ~20s per turn; v1 keeps zero UGC text and tight TikTok pacing. The template's action union can grow game-locally without contract changes.

recommendations.question: Spicy content?
recommendations.recommendation: Launch safe-only (spicyLevel 0). A later 'spicy moves' pack ships as a separate age-gated pack id (intensity 'spicy', tone:'spicy', minAge 18) behind the standard flag, selected via allowedIntensities.
recommendations.why: Physical performance prompts escalate fast; the platform's tone gate (template-architecture §2.7: spicy forces minAge>=18) handles it as pure content ops with no code change.

risks: NEW template = real code, not config-only: reducer + zod schema + 4 client screens + registry entries on both shell and mobile (Cadence A deploy), scheduled after the four designed games per the build-order doc.

Redaction is load-bearing: the offered + chosen prompt texts must never reach dubber/audience/spectator views before reveal, and individual star ballots must NEVER be published (aggregate only) — requires leakedSecrets audits and field-level view-serialization tests like hot-seat's.

The perform phase is unverifiable by the app (phones cannot see the room): an AFK duo just burns 30s. Timers + early 'Done' taps guarantee flow, but fun depends on room energy — mitigate with short performMs and strong host onboarding copy.

Star griefing/inflation (coordinated 1-star trolling or reflex 5-stars): mitigated by the 20-point floor, shared duo score, unscored ratings and unanimity-gated ovation; monitor avg-star and ovation-rate analytics per pack.
Loud by design: live vocal dubbing fails in quiet/public venues — catalog description must set the standup-and-noisy expectation (physical: standup).
Disconnect edges: mover loss voids the turn (no points, feels abrupt — acceptable, mirrors truth-or-dare's active-left rule); dubber loss mid-perform leaves a solo performance still scored as a duo.
Pack sizing: needs >= laps x maxPlayers x promptChoices = 32 prompts per intensity tier at defaults (authoring lint per synthesis §3.5); exhaustion ends the game gracefully via pool_exhausted.
3-player rooms (template floor) have one rater — config tightens to 4; the lobby must gate Start on the effective config minPlayers.
