newTemplateSpec:
TIMED_VERDICT — rotating-spotlight, timed IRL performance, peer-tap adjudication. One module `GameModule<TvState, TvAction, TvView, TvContent>` (`packages/games/timed-verdict/`), id 'timed-verdict', version 1, minPlayers 3, maxPlayers 16. Hosts TWO modes behind `config.mode`: 'puppet' (mime-inverse: secret hidden FROM the spotlight, commanders puppeteer + confirm the guess) and 'blitz' ("Name 3 in 5s": prompt public, peers validate the performance). This resolves template-architecture §7 Q1: blitz moves here; INPUT_GUESS slims to the collab text game. Zero engine amendments — fits the existing contract (phaseKey included) and the shared kit (emptyPlayerMap, Presence/connectedPlayers, allActed, nextActiveSeat, gameOver).

CONFIG (TvConfig, all catalog-overridable via params): { mode: 'puppet'|'blitz'; performMs (30_000 puppet / 5_000 blitz); verdictMs 10_000; revealMs 7_000; scoreboardMs 6_000; scoreboardEvery 4; roundsPerPlayer 1; promptVisibility: 'all'|'others-only' (puppet: 'others-only'); earlyMajorityResolve: boolean (puppet: true); successPoints 100; crewPoints 50 (blitz: 0); speedBonus 50; showCategoryToSpotlight: boolean (puppet: true); verdictThreshold 0.5 }.

STATE (TvState, JSON-safe, null-proto maps): { config; players (roster fixed at init); seatOrder (seeded permutation = shuffle(createRng(seed+'|seats'), players)); seatIndex; turnSeq (monotonic, ++ on each turn entry — ToD pattern); round (lap counter, ++ on rotation wrap); totalTurns = min(players.length × roundsPerPlayer, items.length); items: TvItem[] (shuffle(createRng(seed+'|items'), pack.items), one per turn, current = items[turnCount]); phase: 'perform'|'verdict'|'reveal'|'scoreboard'|'over'; taps: Record<PlayerId,true> /* HIDDEN values; exposed as count only */; verdicts: Record<PlayerId,'yes'|'no'> /* HIDDEN; exposed as counts; NEVER per-voter public, even at reveal */; outcome: 'success-early'|'success-verdict'|'fail'|'void'|null; scores; connected: Presence; sinceScoreboard }.

ACTIONS (zod-validated at DO boundary; enum-only, NO free text → zero moderation surface): { kind:'tap' } (perform phase; sender must be in players, connected, !== spotlight, not already tapped — "Trouvé !"/"Valid") | { kind:'verdict'; vote:'yes'|'no' } (verdict phase; same eligibility; first vote locked, ToD-style). All rejections return the SAME state reference (shell no-op contract).

REDUCER (per phase × event; 'over' short-circuits first):
• perform + tap (eligible): record tap. If earlyMajorityResolve && tapCount >= floor(E/2)+1 where E = connected players minus spotlight (re-evaluated at every event) → resolve 'success-early' → reveal. Else keep state.
• perform + deadline: → verdict; taps carry over as pre-cast 'yes' votes in `verdicts`.
• verdict + verdict-vote (eligible, not yet voted): record. allActed(E, verdicts) → resolve.
• verdict + deadline: resolve with votes in. cast = yes+no; cast===0 → 'fail'; else 'success-verdict' iff yes/cast >= verdictThreshold (ties → success: funny never cruel). E empty at verdict entry → outcome 'void' → reveal immediately (never sit in a phase with zero possible actors).
• resolve scoring (exact): success → spotlight +successPoints (100), +speedBonus (50) iff 'success-early'; EVERY connected non-spotlight player +crewPoints (50) regardless of individual vote (collective scoring kills tap-griefing incentives). fail/void → 0 for all. scores cloned copy-on-write.
• reveal + deadline: enterTurn — seatIndex = nextActiveSeat(seatOrder, seatIndex, connected); turnSeq++; wrapped → round++ and emit analytics 'round_completed' (metrics parity, synthesis §5.4 — the AD TRIGGER is the shell's phaseKey transition to scoreboard:*, not the analytics effect); clear taps/verdicts/outcome. Insert scoreboard when sinceScoreboard<=0 or after the final turn (always one final scoreboard before over). After final scoreboard → over + { type:'gameOver', scores: cloned }.
• scoreboard + deadline: next turn or over.
• playerLeft: connected=false; never deletes roster keys or scores. Leaver === spotlight during perform/verdict → outcome 'void' → reveal (answer shown, 0 pts, analytics 'spotlight_left' — room never stalls on an absent star). Leaver was eligible during perform → re-evaluate early-majority against shrunk E. During verdict → shrink expected, re-check allActed; E now empty → resolve with cast votes or 'void' if none.
• playerRejoined: connected=true, no phase change; eligible again at next evaluation. A disconnected or passive player can NEVER block: every phase is timed, all-acted sets are connected-filtered, spotlight-left voids the turn.

PHASE KEYS / DURATIONS: phaseKey = `${phase}:${turnSeq}` (perform:0, verdict:0, reveal:0, perform:1, …), scoreboard:<turnSeq>, terminal bare 'over'. turnSeq is unique per (phase, turn) — satisfies synthesis §1.6; no secret ever embedded. phaseDurationMs: perform→performMs, verdict→verdictMs, reveal→revealMs, scoreboard→scoreboardMs, over→null.

VIEW REDACTION (the load-bearing surface, puppet mode):
• perform/verdict, viewer === spotlight: { phase, turnSeq, round, totalTurns, spotlight, role:'spotlight', categoryHint (iff showCategoryToSpotlight), tapCount / votesIn+votersExpected (COUNTS only — tension feedback), scores, connected }. NEVER the item's action text or forbidden words.
• perform/verdict, viewer in players && !== spotlight: all of the above PLUS the secret { actionText, forbiddenWords, category, difficulty }, myTapped / myVote (owner-only echo, buffer[viewer] ?? null — never an indexed foreign lookup).
• UNKNOWN/spectator viewer: treated as a potential second device of the spotlight → gets the SPOTLIGHT-redacted view (no secret, no echoes). This is the anti-cheat rule: the secret is shown only to viewers provably in players and provably not the spotlight.
• reveal: actionText, category, outcome, tally {yes,no} (aggregate ONLY — per-voter verdicts are never public, so nobody sees "Marie voted no on you"), gained per player, scores — public to all. This is the payoff beat: the puppet finally learns what they were miming.
• scoreboard/over: standings + scores, public.
• Tests: leakedSecrets audit with secrets = [current item actionText, …forbiddenWords] (namespaced per turn) asserted absent from every spotlight/unknown view during perform/verdict; field-level test that serialized perform views for the spotlight contain no `items`/`taps`/`verdicts` maps; determinism replay test (same seed + same pack version → identical game); edge tests at 3 and 16 players; spotlight-left-mid-perform; rejoin-mid-verdict; item-exhaustion cap.

CONTENT (TvContent): { locale: 'fr'|'en'; items: TvItem[] } — single-locale runtime packs per synthesis §3.1 (bilingual authoring source is split into mime-inverse-fr / mime-inverse-en at publish). puppet TvItem = { id, text (the action), category, forbidden: string[] (3–5 display-only taboo words), difficulty: 1|2|3, tags }. blitz TvItem = { id, text ("Name 3 …"), category, difficulty, tags } (no forbidden). zod: min items >= maxPlayers × roundsPerPlayer (16); recommend 60+. Authoring lint: every action must be safely performable standing in ~2 m² with no props and no physical contact with other players.

phases.description: The puppet stands up, phone in pocket or face-down (their screen shows only the category hint + timer). All commanders see the secret action + forbidden words on their phones and shout imperative instructions IRL ('lift your arms!', 'push it forward!', 'walk in a line!') — never the forbidden words. The puppet obeys and shouts guesses out loud. Any commander taps 'Trouvé !' the moment the puppet names it; when a strict majority of connected commanders has tapped, the phase resolves EARLY as success-early (+50 speed bonus) and jumps straight to reveal. Timeout (deadline) → verdict phase. Disconnected commanders are excluded from the majority denominator; if the puppet disconnects, the turn voids straight to reveal. phaseKey perform:<turnSeq>.

Last call — 'Did [puppet] get it (or close enough)?'. Each connected commander votes Oui/Non (first vote locked; 'Trouvé !' taps from perform carry over as pre-cast Oui). Resolves when all eligible voters have voted OR at deadline with votes in: yes/cast >= 0.5 (ties generous → success). Zero votes cast → fail; zero eligible voters → turn void. Skipped entirely when perform early-resolved. The puppet sees only vote counts, never the secret. phaseKey verdict:<turnSeq>.

The payoff: the answer is revealed to EVERYONE — the puppet finally discovers what they were being puppeteered into. Outcome stamp (TROUVÉ ! / RATÉ / ANNULÉ), aggregate tally only (never per-voter votes), +points animation (puppet +100 [+50 speed], each connected commander +50 on success), next puppet announced. Deadline → next turn's perform, or scoreboard if due (every 4 turns / last turn). phaseKey reveal:<turnSeq>.

Standings beat + the interstitial ad slot (shell fires the ad off the phaseKey transition to scoreboard:*, frequency-capped by remote config). Inserted every scoreboardEvery=4 turns and always once before over. Deadline → next turn or over. phaseKey scoreboard:<turnSeq>.
Terminal, untimed (phaseDurationMs null). Final leaderboard; gameOver effect emitted with a defensively cloned scores map. Reducer is a no-op for all further events.

contentItemShape: One pack item = one mimable everyday action. Shape: { id: string (stable, e.g. 'mi-act-001'); action: {fr,en} — the secret, shown ONLY to commanders (never to the puppet or unknown viewers); category: {fr,en} — soft hint shown to the puppet during perform and to all at reveal; forbidden: {fr: string[], en: string[]} — 3–5 taboo words commanders must not say out loud (display-only honor rule, taboo-style; no speech recognition — deterministic runtime); difficulty: 1|2|3 (1 = guessable in ~15s); spicyLevel: 0|1|2; tags: string[] (e.g. 'physical','household','funny'). Authoring source is bilingual; the publish pipeline splits it into single-locale runtime packs (mime-inverse-fr / mime-inverse-en with data.locale) per the platform's pack convention (cross-game synthesis §3.1). Sizing lint: >= 16 items (maxPlayers × roundsPerPlayer) per difficulty tier; ship 60+. Authoring safety rule: every action performable standing in ~2 m², no props required, no physical contact with other players.

recommendations.question: How does the system know the puppet guessed right? (the brief leaves adjudication open)
recommendations.recommendation: Peer-tap majority, two beats: during the 30s command window any commander taps 'Trouvé !' the moment the puppet shouts the answer (strict majority of connected commanders → instant success + speed bonus); if the timer expires, a 10s last-call verdict vote ('did they get it, or close enough?') with majority-yes and ties → success.
recommendations.why: The guess happens out loud in the room — typing mid-performance breaks the physical comedy and would add the platform's first free-text moderation surface plus a synonym-matching problem ('mowing' vs 'cutting grass'). Peer-tap is enum-only (zero moderation), IRL-native, handles 'close enough' generously (funny never cruel), and reuses the proven ToD verdict pattern. Multiple-choice was rejected: it reduces wild shouted guesses to a menu.

recommendations.question: Is 30 seconds the right command window?
recommendations.recommendation: Yes — keep performMs = 30000 as the catalog default, tunable 20000–45000 via game_config params only (not host-tunable at lobby). Early-majority resolve means good rounds pop at ~15-20s anyway.
recommendations.why: The brief specifies 30s and playtest-tuning belongs in the catalog (a KV edit, no deploy) per the template architecture's catalog-fixed-params default (§7 Q4). Early resolve keeps the median round TikTok-short while 30s gives hard items room to breathe.

recommendations.question: Who scores, and how much?
recommendations.recommendation: Collective on success: puppet +100 (+50 speed bonus if the room confirmed during the command window), EVERY connected commander +50 regardless of their individual vote; fail or void = 0 for all. Scores are match-local; session XP is placement-based per the platform convention.
recommendations.why: Commanders must be rewarded for puppeteering WELL (it is a cooperative comedy machine), but rewarding individual 'Trouvé !' taps would incentivize false-positive tapping. Collective crew points make the only winning move giving genuinely good instructions. 100/50 mirrors hot-seat's spotlight/crowd asymmetry for cross-game familiarity.

recommendations.question: Which template — can an existing one carry it?
recommendations.recommendation: No existing template fits: HOT_SEAT and TRUTH_DARE show the prompt to the active player (mime-inverse needs the exact opposite redaction), SECRET_ROLE has the right redaction but the wrong phase loop. Ship it as NEW:TIMED_VERDICT with mode:'puppet', designed from day one to also host mode:'blitz' ('Name 3 in 5s').
recommendations.why: This resolves template-architecture §7 Q1 (blitz is a timed peer-tap verdict with no typed text — it never belonged in INPUT_GUESS) instead of adding a single-game template: one new module yields two catalog flagships, and INPUT_GUESS slims to the pure collab text game. Build after the designed four so it lands on the battle-tested kit (rotation, allActed, presence, redaction harness).

recommendations.question: How do we stop commanders from just saying the answer out loud?
recommendations.recommendation: A display-only taboo rule: each item ships 3–5 forbidden words rendered prominently on commander screens ('Interdits : tondeuse, pelouse…'); enforcement is social (the room polices itself), plus hold-to-peek on the commander secret card to defeat shoulder-surfing by the standing puppet.
recommendations.why: Speech recognition at runtime would violate the deterministic no-AI-no-API rule and is unnecessary — same-room social enforcement is the genre standard (Taboo). Hold-to-peek addresses the real leak channel, which is physical (the puppet glancing at screens), not the view layer.

recommendations.question: Should the puppet get any hint, and what happens to players who can't or won't perform?
recommendations.recommendation: Show the category hint to the puppet by default (showCategoryToSpotlight: true), and document that seated performance is always acceptable — every pack action must be authorable as doable in place, and a puppet who disconnects or freezes simply voids the turn (0 points, answer revealed, rotation moves on).
recommendations.why: A hopeless flailing puppet stops being funny fast — the category keeps rounds solvable and protects the 'funny never cruel' brand line. Void-and-move-on matches ToD's active-left rule: a passive or absent player must never block the room, and no phase exists without a deadline.

risks: Redaction inversion is the core engineering risk: the secret action + forbidden words must never reach the spotlight viewer OR any unknown viewer (treat unknown ids as a possible second device of the puppet — they get the spotlight-redacted view). Mitigate with per-turn leakedSecrets audits and a field-level test that no items/taps/verdicts maps serialize into spotlight views.

This is NEW template code (Cadence A: deploy required), not a config-only game — the honest effort is a full module build (~1–2 weeks) scheduled after the four designed games, though it amortizes by also delivering 'Name 3 in 5s' as a config.

Verdict griefing: a troll majority can vote down a correct guess (or wave through a wrong one). Mitigations: ties resolve generous, collective scoring removes any points incentive to grief, votes are never publicly attributed (aggregate tally only), and the room's social pressure is the real referee — same accepted posture as truth-or-dare §9 Q3.

Physical/venue constraints: the game needs ~2 m² of safe standing space and a room where shouting is OK; unusable in quiet venues. Pack authoring lint must reject actions requiring props, running, or physical contact with other players (safety + inclusivity), and seated performance must remain legitimate for mobility-impaired players.

Shoulder-surfing is the dominant real-world leak (the standing puppet can glance at commander phones) — UI must default the secret card to hold-to-peek; this is a client design requirement, not enforceable by the engine.
Session length at 16 players: 16 turns × ~45s ≈ 12+ min plus 4 scoreboards; consider capping totalTurns or auto-bumping scoreboardEvery for large rooms (same open call as hot-seat §9 Q2).

Bilingual sample items here are an authoring-source shape; the runtime pack convention is single-locale (data.locale, synthesis §3.1) — the publish pipeline must split FR/EN and keep parallel coverage, or the catalog locale gate will strand one language.

A future spicy pack (age-gated, spicyLevel 1–2) must be a separate pack id behind the tone:'spicy' + minAge>=18 gate and needs explicit consent framing for any physically suggestive actions — recommend launching without it.

taglineEn: One theme, one letter, one word — last one standing takes it all!

phases.description: Round opener: slot-machine reveal of the theme + letter (e.g. 'Les enfants adorent…' + S). alive map resets to all connected players. Deadline -> first survivor's 'say'. Guard at entry: if <2 players connected, go straight to 'over' (gameOver with current scores) — never block the room. phaseKey 'draw:r{round}'.

Shot clock on the spotlit survivor, who SHOUTS a word in the theme starting with the letter (nothing is typed — phones never capture the word). Duration decays per completed lap: max(minSayMs, sayMs - lapInRound*sayDecayPerLapMs) = 8s -> 6.5s -> 5s -> 3.5s -> 3s floor, guaranteeing convergence. Actions: 'wordSaid' (spotlight only, stops the clock -> judge) or 'giveUp' (self-eliminate, skip judge -> result). Deadline OR spotlight disconnect -> auto-elimination (outcome 'timeout'/'left') -> result. At turn entry a disconnected-but-alive player is eliminated for the round (outcome 'left') so an absentee can never win by hiding. phaseKey 'say:t{turnSeq}' (turnSeq global monotonic).

Quick thumbs vote by EVERY other present player — eliminated players join the jury (nobody idle, dilutes rival bias). Action 'judge {vote: valid|reject}', first vote locked, own-vote echo only. Ends early when all eligible voted (all-acted); deadline resolves with votes cast. Rejected iff rejectVotes/castVotes > rejectThreshold (STRICT majority); ties, abstentions and zero votes -> VALID (benefit of the doubt — funny never cruel, anti-griefing). If the eligible-voter set is empty at entry -> auto-valid immediately. Valid: +validWordPoints to spotlight. Rejected: spotlight eliminated. phaseKey 'judge:t{turnSeq}'.

Stamp beat: 'VALIDE ✅' flash or '💥 ÉLIMINÉ' bubble-pop on the player's Bloop, with the anonymous tally (counts only, never who voted what). Deadline -> next alive survivor's 'say' (wrapping the rotation increments lapInRound), or 'roundEnd' when aliveCount<=1 or the hard cap (players × maxTurnsPerRoundFactor turns) is hit. phaseKey 'result:t{turnSeq}'.

Survivor crowned: +survivorPoints to the last one standing (cap case: every still-alive player gets it; zero survivors: no bonus). Emits analytics 'round_completed' — the shell's interstitial-ad boundary. Deadline -> next 'draw' (new theme+letter, alive reset) or 'over' after totalRounds / theme-deck exhaustion. phaseKey 'roundEnd:r{round}'.
Untimed terminal (phaseDurationMs = null). Final leaderboard + gameOver effect with scores. phaseKey 'over'.

contentItemShape: One item = one round card in the AUTHORING/master pack (bilingual; the publisher splits it into per-locale runtime packs '<base>-fr' / '<base>-en' per the platform's one-pack-one-locale convention, template-architecture §2.7): { id: string (stable unique id, the no-repeat key, e.g. "jdt-kids-001"); theme: { fr: string, en: string } (the category sentence shown to everyone, <=80 chars, SHOUTY-readable at arm's length); letters: { fr: string[], en: string[] } (UPPERCASE letters PRE-SCORED OFFLINE as feasible for this theme in that language — gate: >=15 common words exist per (theme, letter, locale); 6–10 letters per locale; the runtime picks one per round via seeded draw with cross-round no-repeat per theme; lists intentionally differ between locales); difficulty: 1|2|3 (drives the 'ascending' round curve: round 1 easy -> later rounds harder); spicy: 0|1|2 (item-level gate; pack tone = max over items; spicy items require an 18+ config sibling); tags?: string[] (freeform, for themed pack curation); exampleWords?: { fr: string[], en: string[] } (authoring/QA evidence for the feasibility gate — NEVER sent to any client during play: it would prime answers). Runtime per-locale item collapses to { id, theme: string, letters: string[], difficulty, spicy, tags? }.

newTemplateSpec:
NEW TEMPLATE: LAST_STANDING (turn-based survival-verdict / battle royale). Pure GameModule<S,A,V,C> per packages/engine/src/types.ts — zero contract amendments, no wall-clock, no ambient RNG, JSON-safe null-proto state, reject-by-same-reference convention. No typed gameplay text => zero new moderation surface (words are spoken aloud in the room; phones are shot clock + jury).

CONFIG (DEFAULT_CONFIG = the game_config.params of this design; all overridable per catalog entry): totalRounds, drawMs, sayMs, sayDecayPerLapMs, minSayMs, judgeMs, resultMs, roundEndMs, validWordPoints, survivorPoints, rejectThreshold, maxTurnsPerRoundFactor, difficultyCurve ('ascending'|'shuffled'), deadPlayersJudge, allowGiveUp.

CONTENT C (runtime, per-locale): { locale: 'fr'|'en', items: [{ id, theme: string, letters: string[], difficulty: 1|2|3, spicy: 0|1|2, tags?: string[] }] }. Authoring lint: items >= totalRounds (recommend >= 3×), every (item, letter) pre-validated for >=15 common words.

STATE S: { config; players: PlayerId[] (roster fixed at init); rotation: PlayerId[] (seeded permutation = lap order); connected: Record<PlayerId,boolean> (presence — synthesis rule: presence ≠ elimination); phase: 'draw'|'say'|'judge'|'result'|'roundEnd'|'over'; round: number (0-based); turnSeq: number (global monotonic, ++ per say entry); lapInRound: number; turnsThisRound: number; spotIndex: number; spotlight: PlayerId; alive: Record<PlayerId,boolean> (per-round elimination, reset at each draw); current: { itemId, theme, letter } | null (public once drawn — it is shouted in the room anyway); HIDDEN themeDeck: string[] (item ids: shuffle within difficulty buckets via createRng(seed+'|themes'), buckets concatenated 1<2<3 when difficultyCurve='ascending'); HIDDEN themeCursor: number; HIDDEN usedLetters: Record<itemId, string[]> (cross-round letter no-repeat); HIDDEN judgeVotes: Record<PlayerId,'valid'|'reject'> (only tallies ever published); lastTurn: { player, outcome: 'valid'|'rejected'|'timeout'|'gaveUp'|'left', tally: { valid: number, reject: number } } | null; roundWinners: PlayerId[]; scores: Record<PlayerId,number>; wordsValidated: Record<PlayerId,number> }.

ACTIONS A (zod-validated at the DO boundary, reducer re-guards — tracer defense in depth): { kind:'wordSaid' } (say phase, spotlight only: stop the clock -> judge, judgeVotes={}); { kind:'giveUp' } (say phase, spotlight only, iff allowGiveUp: alive[spotlight]=false, outcome 'gaveUp' -> result); { kind:'judge', vote:'valid'|'reject' } (judge phase; eligible = present AND !== spotlight AND not yet voted; eliminated players eligible iff deadPlayersJudge; first vote locked; all-acted over the eligible set ends the phase early). All out-of-phase/unknown/duplicate actions silently ignored returning the SAME state reference.

EVENTS / PHASE MACHINE: init -> draw. draw entry: if connectedCount<2 -> over (gameOver, analytics 'room_collapsed'); alive = connected snapshot; item = themeDeck[themeCursor++]; letter = seeded pick createRng(seed+'|letter|'+round+'|'+itemId) over item.letters minus usedLetters[itemId]; deadline -> enterTurn. enterTurn: advance spotIndex through rotation to the next ALIVE player (wrap => lapInRound++); if that player is disconnected, eliminate them immediately (outcome 'left' -> result beat) so an absentee can never outlast the room; turnSeq++, turnsThisRound++, phase='say'. say deadline OR playerLeft(spotlight) -> alive[spotlight]=false, outcome 'timeout'/'left' -> result. judge resolution (all-acted or deadline): cast = votes recorded; cast===0 -> valid; rejected iff rejectCount/cast > rejectThreshold (strict; ties -> valid); valid => scores[spotlight]+=validWordPoints, wordsValidated[spotlight]++, outcome 'valid'; rejected => alive[spotlight]=false, outcome 'rejected'; -> result with tally counts. judge + playerLeft(voter): shrink expected set, resolve if now all-acted, empty set -> auto-valid; playerLeft(spotlight) during judge: resolve with votes cast (claim stands). result deadline: if aliveCount<=1 OR turnsThisRound >= rotation.length×maxTurnsPerRoundFactor -> roundEnd (roundWinners = alive set; each +survivorPoints; zero alive => no bonus); else enterTurn. roundEnd deadline: round++; round>=totalRounds OR themeCursor>=themeDeck.length -> over + gameOver{scores}; else draw. playerRejoined: connected=true only; an eliminated rejoiner stays out for the current round, auto back in next draw. Effects: analytics 'turn_resolved'{outcome}, 'round_completed'{round} at roundEnd (the shell's interstitial boundary — same event name the backbone already consumes), gameOver at over.

phaseDurationMs: draw=drawMs; say=max(minSayMs, sayMs − lapInRound×sayDecayPerLapMs) (pure function of state — decaying shot clock guarantees convergence); judge=judgeMs; result=resultMs; roundEnd=roundEndMs; over=null. phaseKey: 'draw:r{round}' | 'say:t{turnSeq}' | 'judge:t{turnSeq}' | 'result:t{turnSeq}' | 'roundEnd:r{round}' | 'over' — changes exactly when a new deadline must arm; never embeds a secret (theme/letter are public, votes never appear).

VIEW V / REDACTION: common scaffold every phase: { phase, round, totalRounds, turnSeq, rotation, alive, connected, spotlight, current:{theme,letter}, lapInRound, sayMsThisLap, scores, wordsValidated, lastTurn }. say: + youAreSpotlight, canGiveUp (spotlight && allowGiveUp && viewer===spotlight). judge: + youCanVote (viewer present, !==spotlight, not yet voted, deadPlayersJudge gate), myVote (own-vote echo or null — NEVER anyone else's), votesIn (count only), votersExpected (count only). result: + lastTurn (player, outcome, tally COUNTS only — individual votes are never published, even after resolution, mirroring ToD). roundEnd: + roundWinners, pointsAwarded. over: { phase:'over', scores, rotation }. Viewer matrix: spotlight / other-alive / eliminated / disconnected / UNKNOWN id all receive the same public projection differing only in youAreSpotlight/canGiveUp/youCanVote/myVote; unknown viewers get youCanVote=false, myVote=null (spectator-safe per contract). HIDDEN from ALL viewers always: themeDeck, themeCursor, usedLetters, the judgeVotes mapping. Smallest redaction surface of any template — the only secrets are upcoming content and in-flight ballots; redaction audit (leakedSecrets) targets undrawn theme texts + individual votes.

DETERMINISM: all RNG via createRng(seed + suffix) (rotation, theme deck, letter picks); replay() reproduces identical games; chaos/rehydration tests inherit the Plan-2 harness unchanged.

REUSE PAYOFF: 'Name 3 in 5s' (vision concept #8, currently INPUT_GUESS 'blitz') becomes a CONFIG of this template later (params: elimination off / single spotlight per round, judge = green/red peer-tap, sayMs=5000) — resolving template-architecture §7 Q1 by giving the 'TIMED_VERDICT' family a home and shrinking INPUT_GUESS to the collab text game only.

recommendations.question: Le mot est-il tapé sur le téléphone ou dit à l'oral ?
recommendations.recommendation: Dit à l'oral, toujours. Le téléphone n'enregistre jamais le mot : il n'est que chrono + jury (boutons pouce vert/rouge).
recommendations.why: Zéro surface de modération UGC (pas de filtre obscenity à brancher, pas de texte persisté), le fun reste dans la pièce (règle plateforme : les téléphones sont des manettes), et taper un mot sous un chrono de 8s tuerait le rythme.

recommendations.question: Qui valide le mot, et comment trancher les égalités ? (le brief impose le vote de la salle, pas de dictionnaire)
recommendations.recommendation: Rejet uniquement à la majorité STRICTE des votes exprimés (rejectThreshold 0.5, '>' strict) ; égalité, abstentions ou zéro vote => VALIDE. Premier vote verrouillé, pas de changement.
recommendations.why: 'Funny never cruel' : le bénéfice du doute protège le joueur sous pression, empêche le griefing par abstention, et reflète exactement la règle ToD 'ties → done' déjà validée par le design system.

recommendations.question: Que font les joueurs éliminés pendant le reste de la manche ?
recommendations.recommendation: Ils rejoignent le jury (deadPlayersJudge=true) : ils votent sur chaque mot jusqu'à la fin de la manche.
recommendations.why: Règle plateforme 'personne n'est idle' ; en fin de manche le jury élargi dilue le conflit d'intérêt des derniers survivants qui se jugent entre eux ; et regarder en votant, c'est déjà jouer.

recommendations.question: Comment tirer la lettre sans créer des tours injouables ('Les enfants aiment…' + W) ?
recommendations.recommendation: Pas de tirage A–Z uniforme : chaque thème embarque une liste de lettres pré-validées PAR LANGUE (>=15 mots courants par couple thème×lettre, scoré offline par la pipeline IA + cross-check wordlist) ; le runtime fait un tirage seedé sans répétition dans cette liste.
recommendations.why: La faisabilité dépend de la langue et du thème ; c'est exactement le cas d'usage 'IA offline, jamais au runtime' (needsOfflineAiPipeline=true) — l'équité est pré-calculée, le gameplay reste déterministe.

recommendations.question: Comment garantir qu'une manche se termine (battle royale = durée variable) ?
recommendations.recommendation: Double sécurité : le chrono de parole décroît à chaque tour de table (8s, −1.5s/tour de table, plancher 3s) + plafond dur de joueurs×6 tours (atteint => tous les survivants prennent le bonus).
recommendations.why: Le chrono qui rétrécit force mathématiquement la convergence ET fabrique la montée de tension TikTok-native (gros timer qui tremble) ; le plafond est la ceinture de sécurité pour qu'aucune salle ne reste coincée.

recommendations.question: Comment gérer les mots répétés dans la même manche ?
recommendations.recommendation: Par la salle, pas par le moteur : 'Déjà dit = pouce rouge !' affiché en copy UI pendant le vote. Aucun dictionnaire, aucune saisie.
recommendations.why: Les mots sont oraux donc invisibles au moteur ; le brief exclut le dictionnaire ; et policer les répétitions est précisément ce qui rend le jury amusant.

recommendations.question: Quel template ? (aucun existant n'a la boucle de survie)
recommendations.recommendation: NEW:LAST_STANDING (spec complète fournie), conçu pour absorber ensuite 'Name 3 in 5s' (INPUT_GUESS mode blitz) comme simple config. À construire après les quatre jeux désignés, à la place du mode blitz d'INPUT_GUESS.
recommendations.why: TRUTH_DARE a la rotation+verdict mais pas d'élimination ni de prompt persistant ; INPUT_GUESS blitz a spotlight+chrono+peer-tap mais n'existe pas encore. Le doc template-architecture (§7 Q1) demandait déjà si blitz devait devenir un template TIMED_VERDICT : ce jeu y répond — un template construit, deux jeux du catalogue servis.

recommendations.question: Minimum de joueurs ?
recommendations.recommendation: 3 (le module refuse 2), sweet spot 4–10.
recommendations.why: À 2 joueurs, l'unique juge est l'adversaire direct : conflit d'intérêt total (il rejette tout et gagne). À 3+, le jury contient toujours au moins un non-rival.

recommendations.question: Barème exact ?
recommendations.recommendation: +1 point par mot validé (validWordPoints), +3 au dernier survivant de la manche (survivorPoints), jurés non scorés. 3 manches par partie.
recommendations.why: Le +1/mot récompense la participation (être éliminé 5e avec 4 mots validés vaut mieux que 1er sorti), le bonus garde l'enjeu battle-royale, et ne pas scorer les votes garde le jury honnête (leçon ToD §5).

recommendations.question: Du contenu épicé ?
recommendations.recommendation: Lancer 100% safe (spicyLevel 0). Un pack 'thèmes 18+' arrive ensuite comme config sœur tone:'spicy' + minAge 18 (gating catalogue déjà prévu), sans toucher au code.
recommendations.why: Le mécanisme est déjà drôle en safe ; le gating spicy de la plateforme (schema §2.7 : spicy => minAge>=18) couvre l'extension par pur contenu — c'est exactement la promesse template+pack.

risks: Effort honnête : NEW:LAST_STANDING est du vrai code (~1–2 semaines, reducer + client + tests), pas du config-only — à planifier après les quatre jeux désignés ; en compensation il remplace le mode 'blitz' d'INPUT_GUESS et sert deux concepts du catalogue.

Jury rancunier / kingmaking : un éliminé peut voter 'reject' par dépit. Mitigé par majorité stricte + égalité=valide ; à surveiller via analytics (taux de reject des jurés éliminés vs vivants) ; levier futur : pondérer ou couper deadPlayersJudge par config.

Triche à l'honneur : le spotlight peut taper 'Mot lancé !' sans rien dire — c'est précisément ce que le jury sanctionne (le vote EST la validation) ; aucun correctif moteur nécessaire, mais le copy UI doit l'expliquer.

Faisabilité des lettres = qualité-critique : une liste mal scorée crée un tour injouable et le joueur le vit comme une injustice. La gate offline (>=15 mots courants par thème×lettre×langue, LLM + wordlist) est bloquante avant publication, et les listes fr/en divergent volontairement.

Manches longues à 12–16 joueurs (~5–6 min malgré le chrono décroissant) : prévoir une config catalogue grands groupes (totalRounds 2, sayMs 6000) ou plafonner maxPlayers à 12 sur l'entrée catalogue par défaut.
Les mots parlés sont non modérables par construction : on s'appuie sur report/kick/block du lobby ; risque résiduel faible car rien n'est persisté ni diffusé hors de la pièce.

Convention packs mono-locale (synthesis §3.1) vs items bilingues : la pipeline émet un master bilingue puis le publisher le scinde en '<base>-fr'/'<base>-en' — l'étape de split doit vérifier la couverture parallèle des deux locales (gate IA #2).
Déconnexion du spotlight pendant 'say' = élimination de la manche (pas de la partie) ; un rejoigneur revient à la manche suivante — à communiquer clairement en UI pour ne pas paraître punitif.

exampleWords ne doit JAMAIS atteindre un client en jeu (ça soufflerait des réponses) : champ strippé au publish, et l'audit de redaction du template doit le cibler avec themeDeck et les votes individuels.

taglineFr: Un objet secret, zéro mot, 45 secondes pour le faire deviner à la pièce !
taglineEn: One secret object, zero words, 45 seconds to make the room guess it!
newTemplateSpec:
PERFORM_GUESS — performer-secret prompt + IRL performance + claim-credit + group validation vote. One module backs devine-l-objet AND devine-l-action (and future packs: emotions, jobs, movies, songs) as pure game_config + pack variants.

WHY NO EXISTING TEMPLATE FITS: TRUTH_DARE is the nearest skeleton (rotation, active player, group verdict, pass economy) but its promptText is public-by-design in every view; this mechanic REQUIRES performer-only prompt redaction until the claim. It also needs a guesser-credit action (performer taps WHO guessed it) and dual scoring (performer + guesser), which TRUTH_DARE/HOT_SEAT/INPUT_GUESS lack. Making prompt visibility mode-conditional inside TRUTH_DARE is a redaction footgun (synthesis leakedSecrets discipline). New module; maximal reuse of the shared kit (emptyPlayerMap, Presence, allActed, nextActiveSeat, tally, gameOver helper, phaseKey conventions).

CONTRACT FIT: standard GameModule<S,A,V,C> per packages/engine/src/types.ts. Zero new events or effects. phaseKey per synthesis A1. minPlayers 3 (performer + guesser + >=1 validator), maxPlayers 16.

CONFIG (DEFAULT_CONFIG; catalog params is a partial, .strict() in templateParamsSchema): roundsPerPlayer 2 (laps of the rotation); handoffMs 4000; mimeMs 45000; validateMs 12000; revealMs 6000; passesPerPlayer 1; foundPoints 10; fastBonusPoints 5; validateThreshold 0.5; allowedDifficulties ['easy','medium']; bonusFetch false (reserved v1.1 flag, no-op in v1).

CONTENT C (per-locale pack per synthesis §3.1; bilingual authoring source compiles to sibling -fr/-en packs): { locale: 'fr'|'en'; items: Array<{ id: string; object: string; category: string; difficulty: 'easy'|'medium'|'hard'; tags: string[] }> }. Sizing lint: >= maxPlayers x roundsPerPlayer items per allowed difficulty (16x2 = 32+ each).

STATE S (HIDDEN marked):
{ config; players: PlayerId[]; connected: Presence; rotation: PlayerId[] (seeded permutation, createRng(seed+'|rot')); turnIndex: number; turnSeq: number (monotonic, ++ per turn entry); lap: number; performer: PlayerId; phase: 'handoff'|'mime'|'validate'|'reveal'|'over';
  deck: string[] /* HIDDEN: shuffled item ids, createRng(seed+'|deck') */; cursor: number /* HIDDEN */;
  current: { id, object, category, difficulty } | null /* object SECRET to non-performer until validate/reveal */;
  mimeStartedAt: number | null /* event.at at mime entry — powers the fast bonus, deterministic */;
  claim: { guesser: PlayerId; at: number } | null;
  votes: Record<PlayerId,'valid'|'invalid'> /* HIDDEN per-voter; counts-only during validate, tally public at reveal */;
  outcome: 'found'|'contested'|'passed'|'missed'|null;
  passesLeft: Record<PlayerId, number>; scores: Record<PlayerId, number>;
  lastResult: { performer; guesser: PlayerId|null; objectText; categoryText; outcome; tally:{valid,invalid}; points:{performer:number, guesser:number}; fast: boolean } | null }
All maps null-proto (emptyPlayerMap). JSON-safe only.

ACTIONS A (zod at DO boundary + reducer re-guards; rejects return the SAME state reference):
- { kind:'claimFound', guesser: PlayerId } — mime phase, performer only; guesser must be a roster player, present, != performer; one-shot.
- { kind:'pass' } — mime phase, performer only, passesLeft[performer] > 0.
- { kind:'validate', vote:'valid'|'invalid' } — validate phase; eligible = connected AND != performer AND != claim.guesser; first vote locks (no changes).

REDUCER (phase x event; first line: over => same-ref no-op):
- handoff: actions ignored. deadline => draw item (deck[cursor++]; cursor >= deck.length => early 'over' + gameOver + analytics 'pool_exhausted'), set current, mimeStartedAt = event.at, phase='mime'.
- mime: claimFound(performer, valid guesser) => claim={guesser, at:event.at}; votes=empty; phase='validate'. pass(performer, passesLeft>0) => outcome='passed'; passesLeft--; build lastResult (points 0/0); phase='reveal'. deadline => outcome='missed'; lastResult; phase='reveal' (no pass burnt). playerLeft(performer) => outcome='missed'; phase='reveal'. Everything else ignored.
- validate: validate by eligible not-yet-voted => record; if allActed(eligible, votes) => resolve. deadline => resolve with cast votes. RESOLUTION: cast=0 => valid (benefit of the doubt); else valid iff validCount/cast >= validateThreshold (ties => valid). valid => outcome='found'; fast = (claim.at - mimeStartedAt) <= mimeMs/2; award = foundPoints + (fast ? fastBonusPoints : 0); scores[performer]+=award; scores[claim.guesser]+=award. invalid => outcome='contested'; 0/0. Then lastResult; phase='reveal'; analytics 'validated' {outcome, valid, invalid}. playerLeft(voter) shrinks eligible (resolve if remaining all-acted; empty set => valid). performer/guesser leaving never aborts — votes decide.
- reveal: actions ignored. deadline => enterTurn: nextActiveSeat(rotation, turnIndex, connected) skips disconnected seats; wrapped => lap++ and, if not ending, emit analytics 'round_completed' {round: lap} (the shell's interstitial ad boundary, synthesis §5.4); lap >= roundsPerPlayer => phase='over' + gameOver(cloned scores); else turnSeq++, reset turn fields, phase='handoff'.
- playerLeft/playerRejoined any phase: flip connected only; seat greyed never freed; scores/passes preserved; rejoiner takes their seat next lap. A disconnected or passive player can never block: every phase is deadline-driven and validate uses connected-filtered allActed.

VIEW V — redaction matrix (viewers: P performer, G credited guesser, O other player, S spectator/disconnected, U unknown id — O/S/U always identical, non-leaking):
- common (all phases): { phase, turnSeq, lap, roundsPerPlayer, rotation, performer, connected, scores, passesLeft }.
- handoff: all: youArePerformer flag; no secret exists yet in views (item drawn at mime entry).
- mime: P: + { objectText: current.object, categoryText, canPass, claimableTargets (present roster minus self) }. O/S/U: + { categoryText ONLY, guessing prompt }. The secret is gated on viewer === performer — never an indexed lookup.
- validate: ALL: objectText now public (the claim is on the table — voters must know the object), claimedGuesser, votesIn/votersExpected COUNTS only, youCanVote, youVoted = own echo or null (never others' votes).
- reveal: ALL identical: full lastResult incl. public tally {valid, invalid} and points.
- over: { phase:'over', scores }.
leakedSecrets audit secrets = current.object for every non-performer viewer during handoff/mime + ALL undrawn deck objects in every phase + in-flight individual votes during validate. phaseKey/analytics strings NEVER embed item ids or object text.

phaseDurationMs: handoff=handoffMs; mime=mimeMs; validate=validateMs; reveal=revealMs; over=null.
phaseKey: `${phase}:${turnSeq}` (turnSeq not lap — many turns per lap, synthesis §1.6 uniqueness rule); terminal bare 'over'.

DETERMINISM: all randomness from seed (rotation + deck shuffles); fast-bonus math uses server event.at deltas only; no Date.now/Math.random; replay() must reproduce identical games with the same pinned pack version.

PLATFORM INTEGRATION: templateIdSchema grows 'PERFORM_GUESS'; templateParamsSchema adds the params above; AI gate validates pack schema + sizing + profanity scan as for all packs. One client GameScreen: performer spotlight card (secret object + tap-the-roster claim grid + Pass pip), guesser card (category chip + 'shout your guesses!' + timer ring), validate chips (fair / no way), reveal card (stamp FOUND/PASSED/MISSED/CONTESTED + points burst + next performer). Build AFTER the shared kit + one shipped turn-based game (TRUTH_DARE) so rotation/verdict/redaction patterns are battle-tested.

phases.description: Spotlight the next performer: 'Leve-toi, {nickname} !' / 'Stand up, {nickname}!'. No actions; the deadline auto-advances into mime (the secret object is drawn at mime entry). phaseKey handoff:{turnSeq}.

The performer's phone privately shows the secret object; everyone else sees only the public category chip + timer and shouts guesses out loud in the room. The performer taps the avatar of the first correct guesser (claimFound) or Pass (1 per game). Deadline or performer disconnect = MISSED (no pass burnt) straight to reveal — a passive performer never blocks the room. phaseKey mime:{turnSeq}.

Reached only after a claim. The object is revealed to ALL; every present player except the performer and the credited guesser votes 'C'etait bon ? / Fair?' (the brief's vote idea, repurposed as anti-cheat). Resolves on all-acted or deadline: >=50% of cast votes = valid; ties and zero votes = valid (benefit of the doubt); empty voter set auto-validates. phaseKey validate:{turnSeq}.

Result card for everyone: the object + outcome stamp (FOUND +10/+10, fast bonus +5/+5 each if claimed in the first half of the timer; PASSED / MISSED / CONTESTED = 0) + updated scores + next performer. Deadline advances to the next turn; a lap wrap emits round_completed (the shell's interstitial ad boundary); after roundsPerPlayer laps, 'over' + gameOver with final scores. phaseKey reveal:{turnSeq}.

contentItemShape: One object card (bilingual authoring source; the pack compiler splits it into sibling single-locale packs devine-l-objet-fr / devine-l-objet-en per synthesis §3.1): { id: string — stable unique id, e.g. 'obj-easy-001' (no-repeat draw key + per-entry report key); object: { fr: string, en: string } — the SECRET object name: visible only to the performer during mime, revealed to everyone at validate/reveal; category: { fr: string, en: string } — public hint chip shown to all players at mime start (keeps rounds fast); difficulty: 'easy' | 'medium' | 'hard' — drawable only if listed in params.allowedDifficulties; tags: string[] — curation metadata, e.g. 'inRoomLikely', 'household', 'tech', 'party'; spicy: 0 | 1 | 2 — item tone, must match the pack's tone (default pack is all 0; a spicy object pack ships as a separate age-gated pack).

recommendations.question: The brief's open question: should there be an extra vote 'pour être sûr de l'existence de l'objet dans la pièce' (to be sure the object exists in the room)?
recommendations.recommendation: Do NOT ship a standalone pre-mime existence vote. Repurpose the vote idea as the post-claim 12s group VALIDATION vote (the validate phase), and curate the default pack toward common-room objects (tag 'inRoomLikely').
recommendations.why: Objects come from a pre-moderated content pack, so physical presence in the room is unnecessary for the mime to work; a pre-round existence vote adds a dead ~10s beat to EVERY turn with no stakes, killing the TikTok pacing. The validation vote keeps every non-performer engaged each turn and catches the only real cheats (crediting a friend who never guessed, saying the word out loud) — it delivers exactly the assurance the co-founder wanted ('être sûr') where it actually matters.

recommendations.question: Should the secret object come from a content pack, or be freely chosen by the performer from real objects in the room?
recommendations.recommendation: Pack-driven secret objects.
recommendations.why: Deterministic runtime (hard constraint), zero free-text moderation surface (a player-typed object would be the platform's first gameplay-text input before the INPUT_GUESS moderation path is hardened), curated bilingual comedy, and difficulty tiers. Room-chosen objects also let the performer pick something trivially visible, deflating the game.

recommendations.question: Is there a salvageable physical twist from the existence-vote idea?
recommendations.recommendation: Reserve a 'bonusFetch' param (default false, no-op in v1): after a validated find, an 8s beat where the first player to physically brandish a matching object earns +5, confirmed by one group tap. Ship in v1.1 only if playtests want more chaos.
recommendations.why: It preserves the room-physical kernel of the co-founder's idea — a real in-room moment phones can't fake, fully on-brand — but it adds a 5th phase and a second mini-vote per turn; pacing must be playtested first.

recommendations.question: Should devine-l-objet share a template with the sibling devine-l-action brief ('même mécanique')?
recommendations.recommendation: Yes — build PERFORM_GUESS once; devine-l-action and devine-l-objet ship as two game_configs + two content packs on it (action pack vs object pack; objet adds the public category chip, action can leave category empty or use verb groups).
recommendations.why: The brief says the mechanic is identical; one module avoids a near-duplicate reducer/client screen and doubles the catalog leverage of the new template (future packs: emotions, jobs, movies, songs).

recommendations.question: Should harder objects score more points?
recommendations.recommendation: Flat 10/10 (+5/+5 fast bonus) in v1; revisit difficulty multipliers (e.g. hard = 15) after playtest data.
recommendations.why: Flat scoring stays legible at a party and avoids fairness arguments; the fast bonus already rewards skill, and the cross-game session leaderboard is placement-based anyway (synthesis §1.7), so internal scale inflation buys nothing.

risks: NEW template = real code (Cadence A: module + client GameScreen + server/mobile registry + deploy), not config-only — roughly a one-week build on the shared kit; sequence it after the kit/phaseKey baseline and ideally after TRUTH_DARE ships, so rotation + verdict + redaction patterns are battle-tested.

Redaction is the load-bearing risk: current.object must never reach a non-performer view, phaseKey, or analytics string before the claim/reveal; mandatory leakedSecrets audit over the undrawn deck, the in-flight object, and individual validate votes.

IRL honor system: the engine cannot observe the mime; a hostile room can grief via 'invalid' votes — mitigated by ties-to-valid, zero-votes-to-valid, and unscored votes ('funny never cruel': no negative points anywhere); monitor the contested-rate analytic and revisit verdictThreshold if abuse shows.
Must converge with the parallel devine-l-action design on ONE shared PERFORM_GUESS template and pack schema before either game builds — otherwise the platform gets two near-duplicate modules.

Pacing at large rooms: 16 players x 2 laps ≈ 32 turns ≈ 30+ min; the game_config should cap maxPlayers at ~12 or auto-scale roundsPerPlayer to 1 at 10+ players (host-tunable rounds is template-architecture §7 Q4).

Inclusivity: miming excludes shy or low-mobility players; the 1-pass economy is the relief valve and pass/missed cost 0 points — copy must never mock a missed turn; consider an accessibility variant (describe-without-the-word) as a future pack/param.

Bilingual authoring: runtime packs are single-locale (synthesis §3.1), so the bilingual {fr,en} authoring source must compile into parallel -fr/-en sibling packs with full coverage, enforced by the AI-gate pack validation.

taglineFr: Toute la pièce suit une règle secrète. Sauf toi. Démasque-la avant la fin du chrono.
taglineEn: The whole room is following a secret rule. Except you. Crack it before the clock runs out.
newTemplateSpec:
RULE_HUNT — inverted social deduction: 1–2 PUBLIC detectives hunt a secret behavioral rule the rest of the room must obey until the clock expires.

WHY A NEW TEMPLATE (per template-architecture §3 honesty test): SECRET_ROLE (impostor) is the nearest neighbor but shares almost nothing at the reducer level. Here roles are PUBLIC (announced at briefing — faithful to the classic parlor game), the secret belongs to the MAJORITY, the main loop is a pausable free-play clock with interrupt-driven sub-phases (accusation tribunal, multiple-choice guess), guessing is a deterministic index compare against pre-computed decoys, and the win condition is clock survival. No clue rotation, no parity math, no simultaneous elimination vote over the whole roster. Forcing this onto SECRET_ROLE params would rewrite its entire reducer; this clears the new-template bar.

1. MODULE IDENTITY
GameModule id 'rule-hunt', version 1, minPlayers 4, maxPlayers 16. Pure TS per packages/engine/src/types.ts: no Date.now / Math.random; all randomness via createRng(seed); all timing via event `at` timestamps + phaseDurationMs. Reuses the shared kit (emptyPlayerMap, Presence/connectedPlayers, allActed, tally, gameOver). No free text at runtime (nothing for the profanity filter; the guess is a tap).

2. CONFIG (DEFAULT_CONFIG = the catalog params, see params field)
detectiveCount 'auto' = 1 detective for 4–7 players, 2 for 8–16 (pure function of roster size, impostor-table style).

3. CONTENT SCHEMA
ContentPack<RuleHuntContent> { locale:'fr'|'en', tone?:'classic'|'spicy', items: RuleItem[] } (runtime packs are single-locale per synthesis §3.1; authoring source is bilingual — the offline pipeline emits sibling -fr/-en packs). RuleItem per contentItemShape. Authoring lints: items.length >= totalRounds (runtime caps totalRounds = min(config.totalRounds, items.length), tracer-style); EXACTLY candidateCount-1 (=7) decoys per item; decoys same category as the rule, mutually distinct under normalizeText, all profanity-scanned offline.

4. init(seed, players, content)
rng = createRng(seed). items = shuffle(rng, content.data.items). detectiveOrder = shuffle(rng, players). Round-r detectives = next detectiveCount ids from detectiveOrder, consecutive with wraparound (fair rotation; a disconnected scheduled detective is skipped forward at round start). Per round: candidates = shuffle(roundRng forked from seed+round, [item.rule, ...item.decoys]) -> candidateTexts (publishable) + trueCandidateIndex (HIDDEN until reveal). State: phase 'briefing', round 0, scores 0, connected all true, eliminated all false, accusationsLeft = accusationsPerPlayer for followers, teamGuessesLeft = teamGuesses, usedCandidates [], liveRemainingMs = liveMs, liveSeg 0, interruptSeq 0. Effects: analytics 'rule_match_started' { players, detectives }.

5. STATE SHAPE (JSON-safe, null-proto maps; HIDDEN = never in any non-owner view)
phase: 'briefing'|'live'|'tribunal'|'guess'|'reveal'|'over'; round; config; players: PlayerId[]; connected: Presence; detectiveOrder: PlayerId[] (never in views — future rotation is a spoiler); detectives: PlayerId[] (PUBLIC by design); eliminated: Record<PlayerId,boolean> (PUBLIC; round-local; conviction-only, never via disconnect); itemIndex; candidateTexts: string[]; trueCandidateIndex: number (HIDDEN until reveal — the round's secret, together with the rule text vs detectives); ackRule: Record<PlayerId,boolean>; liveRemainingMs: number (the pause/resume bank); segmentStartedAt: number (`at` of the event that (re)entered live); liveSeg: number; interruptSeq: number; accusationsLeft: Record<PlayerId,number>; teamGuessesLeft: number; usedCandidates: number[] (PUBLIC, greyed in grid); tribunal: null | { accused, accuser, votes: Record<PlayerId,boolean> /* HIDDEN buffer */ }; guess: null | { guesser: PlayerId }; lastTribunal: null | { accused, accuser, guilty, tally:{guilty,notGuilty}, abstained: PlayerId[] } (PUBLIC); lastOutcome: null | { kind:'guessed'|'timeUp', guesser?, pickedIndex?, perfect: boolean, trueIndex, ruleText } (PUBLIC on reveal); infractions: number; scores; endReason: null|'finished'|'roomCollapsed'.

6. ACTIONS (zod at DO boundary; wrong-phase/non-eligible/duplicate actions are inert = same state reference, per the contract's no-op rule)
{ kind:'ackRule' } (briefing; connected followers) | { kind:'accuse'; target } (live; follower with accusationsLeft>0; target = non-eliminated follower != self) | { kind:'tribunalVote'; guilty: boolean } (tribunal; eligible voters; first vote locks) | { kind:'openGuess' } (live; any detective; teamGuessesLeft>0) | { kind:'pickCandidate'; index } (guess; the opening detective only; 0<=index<candidateCount, index not in usedCandidates).

7. PHASE MACHINE (phase x event; every phase has a deadline behavior — no player can block the room)
- briefing (briefingMs=20s): ackRule buffered; allActed(connected followers, ackRule) -> live (segmentStartedAt = event.at). deadline -> live regardless.
- live (phaseDurationMs = state.liveRemainingMs): accuse(valid) -> bank the clock: liveRemainingMs = max(0, liveRemainingMs - (at - segmentStartedAt)); interruptSeq++; accusationsLeft[accuser]--; -> tribunal. openGuess(valid) -> bank clock; interruptSeq++; -> guess. deadline -> reveal kind 'timeUp' (perfect = infractions===0).
- tribunal (tribunalMs=25s): voters = connected followers, not eliminated, != accused (accuser may vote; detectives NEVER vote — they don't know the rule). First vote locks; allActed(eligible, votes) or deadline -> resolve: guilty iff guiltyCount > notGuiltyCount (tie/zero = not guilty — funny never cruel). Guilty -> eliminated[accused]=true; infractions++. Publish lastTribunal (aggregate tally + abstainers ONLY; per-voter ballots never serialized). Then: if connected non-eliminated followers < 2 OR liveRemainingMs <= 0 -> reveal('timeUp'); else resume live (segmentStartedAt = resolving event.at; liveSeg++).
- guess (guessMs=20s): pickCandidate from guess.guesser -> teamGuessesLeft--. index === trueCandidateIndex -> reveal kind 'guessed' (detectives win the round early). Else usedCandidates.push(index); resume live (liveSeg++) or reveal('timeUp') if clock empty. deadline -> attempt SPENT with no pick (kills pause-stalling abuse), resume live / reveal if clock empty.
- reveal (revealMs=12s): inert to actions; scoring applied on entry + analytics 'round_completed' (the spec-§8.6 ad-cue name; the interstitial itself fires off the shell's phaseKey diff, never off analytics). deadline -> next round (round++, rotate detectives, next item, reset round-locals: eliminated, ackRule, accusationsLeft, teamGuessesLeft, usedCandidates, liveRemainingMs=liveMs, liveSeg=0, interruptSeq=0) -> briefing; or if round+1===totalRounds -> over + gameOver(cloned scores).
- over: untimed (phaseDurationMs null), globally inert.
- playerLeft (any phase): connected[p]=false ONLY (seat greyed; never eliminates, never rescores). All resolution gates use connected-filtered expected sets, so a disconnect can never stall past a deadline. Accused leaves mid-tribunal -> vote proceeds normally (no auto-conviction). Guesser leaves mid-guess -> resolve as deadline (attempt spent, resume). All detectives disconnected -> round simply runs out its clock (followers cruise). Room-collapse: at any resolution point, connectedPlayers < 3 -> over, endReason 'roomCollapsed', gameOver(current scores). playerRejoined: connected[p]=true; resumes acting if the phase is still open.

8. phaseKey / phaseDurationMs
Keys: 'briefing:r{r}' | 'live:r{r}:s{seg}' | 'tribunal:r{r}:i{n}' | 'guess:r{r}:i{n}' | 'reveal:r{r}' | 'over'. liveSeg increments on every resume so the shell re-arms the SHORTER remaining duration; interruptSeq makes every tribunal/guess instance unique (synthesis §1.6 uniqueness rule). No secrets in keys. Durations: briefing/tribunal/guess/reveal from config; live = state.liveRemainingMs; over = null. CLOCK DETERMINISM: the pause/resume bank uses only event `at` arithmetic (interrupt.at - segmentStartedAt, clamped >= 0) — fully replay-deterministic; no wall clock ever enters the module.

9. SCORING (exact; applied on reveal entry; accumulates across rounds within the match; shell owns cross-game session XP via placement, synthesis §1.7)
- kind 'guessed': each detective +4; each surviving (non-eliminated) follower +1; eliminated followers +0.
- kind 'timeUp' AND perfect (zero convictions — the brief's "ni enfreinte ni devinée" full win): each follower +3; each detective +1 (consolation).
- kind 'timeUp' AND not perfect: each surviving follower +2; each eliminated follower +1 (they took the fall — funny never cruel); each detective +1.
- Tribunals and wrong guesses move no points directly: their cost is the spent token/attempt and the information they leak.
- gameOver scores are cloned, never aliasing live state (tracer invariant).

10. VIEW + REDACTION (discriminated union on phase; spectator-safe for unknown viewers)
Base envelope: round/totalRounds, seats[{id, connected, eliminated, isDetective}] (roles PUBLIC), scores, myRole ('detective'|'follower'|null for unknown viewers), iAmEliminated, myAccusationsLeft, teamGuessesLeft, usedCandidates.
- myRule (the secret rule text): followers only — INCLUDING eliminated followers (they knew it); null for detectives and unknown viewers until reveal.
- briefing: acked booleans only.
- tribunal: accused/accuser public; hasVoted booleans public; myVote = votes[viewer] ?? null (owner echo only); raw votes map never serialized; aggregate tally only after resolution via lastTribunal.
- guess: candidates (all candidateCount texts, seed-shuffled, byte-identical order for EVERY viewer — no per-viewer reorder side channel) visible to all ROSTER players (followers know the rule anyway; the room sweats with the detective) but OMITTED for unknown viewers (a spectator must not get a 1-in-8 shortlist of the secret); guesser/iAmGuessing public; trueCandidateIndex NEVER serialized pre-reveal.
- reveal: lastOutcome public (rule text now public to everyone), lastTribunal public.
- over: standings + endReason.
Redaction invariants (each -> a test + leakedSecrets audit, impostor-style): (1) pre-reveal, no detective/unknown view contains the rule text EXCEPT undistinguished inside the guess-phase candidates array for roster players (audit trueCandidateIndex instead for grid states); (2) trueCandidateIndex never appears pre-reveal; (3) candidates order identical across viewers; (4) per-voter tribunal ballots never serialized; (5) detectiveOrder never in any view; (6) unknown viewer: myRule=null, candidates omitted, myVote=null. leakedSecrets config: secret = rule text with owners = followers (skip '' / never feed empty values, synthesis §5.9).

11. EFFECTS: analytics 'rule_match_started', 'tribunal_resolved' {guilty}, 'guess_attempted' {correct}, 'round_completed' (reveal entry); gameOver at over. No new Effect or GameEvent types — fits the contract with zero amendments.

12. templateParamsSchema addition (.strict()): RULE_HUNT: { totalRounds 1..8?, briefingMs 10k..30k?, liveMs 120k..300k?, tribunalMs 15k..40k?, guessMs 10k..30k?, revealMs 8k..20k?, detectiveCount 'auto'|1|2?, teamGuesses 1..5?, candidateCount 6|8|10?, accusationsPerPlayer 0..3? }.

13. TEST PLAN (mirrors impostor Appendix B): init determinism (same seed -> same item/detective/candidate order); clock-bank arithmetic incl. interrupt-at-deadline edge + replay equality (engine replay(), identical pack version); tribunal lock/eligibility/tie->not-guilty/deadline-partial-votes; guess correct/wrong/timeout-spends/used-index-inert; scoring matrix (guessed / perfect / not-perfect); presence (disconnect can't stall, accused-leaves, guesser-leaves, all-detectives-leave, room collapse < 3); redaction invariants 1–6.

phases.description: Detectives are publicly announced; every follower privately reads the secret rule on their phone and taps OK. Ends early when all connected followers have acked; deadline starts the round regardless (an absent player never blocks).

The main clock — free play in the room: followers obey the rule out loud / physically, detectives observe and interrogate. The clock PAUSES on interrupts (accusation -> tribunal, detective guess -> guess) and resumes with the banked remainder. Deadline -> reveal (followers survive the round).

Interrupt sub-phase: a follower spent their accusation token on a suspected rule-breaker. Eligible followers (connected, not eliminated, not the accused; detectives excluded) secretly vote guilty/not-guilty; first vote locks. Majority of cast votes convicts -> accused eliminated (+1 infraction, a juicy clue for the detectives). Tie, zero votes, or deadline-with-partial-votes -> not guilty. Then resume live.

Interrupt sub-phase: a detective opens the guess grid (8 candidate rules: the true one + 7 pre-computed decoys, seed-shuffled, wrong picks greyed) and locks ONE. Correct -> round ends, detectives win. Wrong -> candidate greyed, team attempt spent, resume live. Deadline -> attempt spent with no pick (anti-stalling), resume live.

The rule is shown to everyone, with the outcome (guessed / time-up perfect / time-up with infractions) and the exact point awards. Deadline -> next round with rotated detectives and a fresh rule, or over after the last round.

Untimed terminal standings (phaseDurationMs returns null); gameOver effect emitted with cloned final scores; shell shows leaderboard, fires the interstitial off the phaseKey transition, offers rematch.

contentItemShape: One RuleItem = { id: string (kebab, e.g. "rh-no-yes"); category: 'gesture'|'verbal'|'social'; difficulty: 'easy'|'medium'|'hard'; spicy: 0|1|2 (item rating; pack tone gates it — spicy items only in age-gated packs); rule: { fr: string, en: string } (the secret rule, imperative voice, <= 120 chars per locale; shown privately to followers and publicly at reveal); decoys: Array<{ fr: string, en: string }> of EXACTLY candidateCount-1 = 7 entries — offline-AI-generated plausible alternates: same category as the rule, observably-distinct behaviors, mutually distinct under normalizeText, profanity-scanned at authoring. The runtime guess grid is the seeded shuffle of [rule, ...decoys]. All player-visible strings are bilingual {fr,en} at authoring; the offline pipeline splits the source into sibling single-locale FR/EN packs (synthesis §3.1) so the runtime loader stays single-locale.

recommendations.question: The brief says "un ou deux joueurs" — how many detectives?
recommendations.recommendation: Auto-scale: 1 detective for 4–7 players, 2 for 8–16 (param detectiveCount:'auto', overridable to 1|2). Two detectives share one pool of 3 guesses and confer out loud.
recommendations.why: In small rooms a second detective leaves too few followers to behave 'normally'; in big rooms one detective cannot watch 12+ people, and two detectives whispering theories is great party content. Mirrors the impostor role-count table pattern.

recommendations.question: The brief leaves "X minutes" open — how long is the live clock?
recommendations.recommendation: 180 seconds default (liveMs param, 120k–300k range). A full round lands ~4.5 min with briefing + ~1 tribunal + ~1 guess + reveal; a 3-round session is ~13 min.
recommendations.why: TikTok-native pacing: 3 minutes is long enough for the rule to surface several times but short enough that followers can hold the act and an eliminated player is never benched for long.

recommendations.question: The brief implies the app judges whether the rule "a été devinée" — how, with no AI at runtime?
recommendations.recommendation: Multiple-choice guess grid: 8 candidates (true rule + 7 pre-generated decoys), deterministic index compare. UI copy encourages the detective to shout the guess out loud before locking it.
recommendations.why: Free-text rule matching is non-deterministic and impossible to score fairly; a decoy grid is deterministic, instant, and dramatic. Decoy generation/scoring is exactly what the offline AI pipeline is for (needsOfflineAiPipeline=true, gated per template-architecture §6).

recommendations.question: How are rule infractions detected when the app cannot see the room?
recommendations.recommendation: Follower self-policing: each follower gets 1 accusation token; an accusation opens a 25s tribunal where followers vote guilty/not-guilty; conviction eliminates the breaker.
recommendations.why: The honor system needs a social check, and the tribunal is the game's genius loop: every conviction is a giant clue for the detectives ('what did Léa just do?'), creating the core tension between enforcing the rule and feeding the enemy information.

recommendations.question: Strict brief reading: does ONE broken rule make the followers lose outright?
recommendations.recommendation: No — soften: a confirmed infraction eliminates the breaker and downgrades the team award (perfect +3 -> survivors +2 / eliminated +1). Only a correct guess ends the round early. The brief's full condition ('ni enfreinte ni devinée') is preserved as the top-prize perfect round.
recommendations.why: Instant team loss on one slip is rage-inducing and anti 'funny never cruel'; the perfect-round bonus keeps the brief's double condition meaningful while keeping every round playable to the end.

recommendations.question: Do detectives vote in tribunals?
recommendations.recommendation: No. They spectate the tribunal with hasVoted booleans only.
recommendations.why: They don't know the rule, so their vote is pure noise and a griefing vector; watching WHO gets accused and convicted is itself the clue they're owed. Their exclusion is public, which is fine — roles are public by design.

recommendations.question: Hidden or public detective identity?
recommendations.recommendation: Public, announced at briefing.
recommendations.why: Faithful to the classic parlor game the brief describes ('ils devront la trouver' — the seekers are known); hidden seekers would collapse this into impostor/SECRET_ROLE territory and kill the interrogation dynamic where the room performs AT the detective.

recommendations.question: Bilingual {fr,en} items vs the platform's single-locale pack rule (synthesis §3.1)?
recommendations.recommendation: Author bilingual source items (as sampled); the offline pipeline emits sibling single-locale packs (trouvez-la-regle-fr / -en); the shell resolves locale at startGame per the pack-family convention (template-architecture §2.7).
recommendations.why: Keeps the runtime loader and init() locale-free as ruled by the synthesis, while authoring/QA stays one bilingual source of truth.

risks: New template = real code (Cadence A): reducer + mobile GameScreen + server/mobile registry entries + deploy. It cannot ship as a config of an existing template; schedule it after the four designed games (alongside or after INPUT_GUESS) so it lands on the battle-tested kit.

Decoy quality is load-bearing: too-obvious decoys make the 8-grid trivial (detectives win on guess #1), near-duplicates make a correct observation unguessable. The offline pipeline must score plausibility AND mutual distinctness, with the human playtest gate before enabled=true (template-architecture §6 stages 1–5).

Honor-system core: nothing technically stops a follower from silently ignoring the rule; enforcement is purely social (tribunal). Accepted as party-game trust, but the round intro copy must sell 'coûte que coûte' hard.

Griefing via accusations: capped at 1 token per follower per round and a majority tribunal, but a colluding clique can still eliminate someone unfairly — mitigated by the elimination consolation point (+1) and short rounds; monitor tribunal_resolved analytics for abuse patterns.

The pause/resume clock (banked liveRemainingMs from event `at` arithmetic) is the trickiest determinism surface in the platform so far: needs explicit replay tests, clamping at the interrupt-vs-deadline race, and the resume-with-tiny-remainder edge.

Spectator/redaction leak surface: the guess grid CONTAINS the true rule, so it must be omitted for unknown viewers, trueCandidateIndex must never serialize pre-reveal, candidate order must be byte-identical across viewers, and per-voter tribunal ballots must never leave hidden state — each is a leakedSecrets-audited test.

Eliminated-player boredom: they keep the rule on screen and spectate tribunals but cannot act for the rest of the round (max ~3 min); rounds are short and elimination resets every round, but watch abandon analytics on eliminated players.
All-detectives-disconnect edge gives followers a free cruise to the round win; acceptable (rare, self-inflicted) but the room-collapse guard (connected < 3 -> over) must cover the worst case.
